title: 基于拓扑的量子态分解与计算
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state decomposition method based on topological properties. Traditional approaches often rely on complex quantum circuits, while topological methods offer a more intrinsic and physical description. We propose a method that leverages topological structures to efficiently decompose quantum states and facilitate quantum state computation and evolution. The core mechanism involves constructing and manipulating topological structures to represent the quantum state, enabling optimized calculations and manipulations. The advantages of this approach include improved efficiency, reduced complexity, and a deeper understanding of quantum information. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through theoretical analysis and preliminary numerical simulations.

title: Neural Network Topology-Driven Self-Organizing Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network learning, termed topology-driven self-organizing learning. The core idea is to mimic the biological neural network's inherent structural properties – namely, the physical connections between neurons and localized synaptic plasticity – to achieve more efficient and robust learning. We employ a Self-Organizing Map (SOM) algorithm, augmented with a dynamically generated topological network, to facilitate this process. Neurons adapt their connection weights based on input data, while the network's topology undergoes self-adaptive adjustments mirroring the learning patterns. This integration of topology and learning offers a fundamentally new approach, promising networks with enhanced biological relevance and performance. The key contributions lie in the dynamic topological evolution guided by the learning process and the utilization of a SOM framework for distributed representation and adaptation. The resulting network exhibits superior learning capabilities compared to traditional self-organizing methods that often neglect the influence of the underlying physical connections and network topology. We demonstrate through theoretical analysis and a conceptual framework the potential of this approach to create neural networks that are both more efficient and more resilient to noise and changing environments.

title: Algorithmic Coherence in Deep Learning via Feedback Loops
abstract: This paper explores the potential of employing feedback loops within deep neural networks to enhance generalization and stability. Current approaches frequently concentrate on optimizing individual parameters, neglecting the dynamic nature of the learning process. We propose an algorithmic framework centered on a continuous evaluation and adjustment mechanism, driven by a feedback loop, designed to iteratively refine the network's understanding and improve its ability to generalize to unseen data. The core of this approach lies in establishing a system where the network's output is directly evaluated against a predefined metric, and adjustments are made to the learning parameters based on this assessment. This paper details the proposed algorithm, its theoretical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its potential to mitigate the inherent challenges of deep learning.

title: Adaptive Quantum State Prediction Modeling
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to quantum state prediction, introducing an adaptive quantum state prediction model that dynamically adjusts its parameters based on the predicted state. Traditional methods are static and often struggle to accurately predict the states of complex quantum systems. Our model leverages quantum state evolution and feedback to achieve significantly improved accuracy and speed, offering a real-time prediction capability. We detail the model's architecture, the feedback mechanism, and the resulting performance improvements through theoretical analysis and experimental validation. The core claim of this work is that a self-adaptive quantum state prediction model, driven by dynamic parameter adjustment, can dramatically enhance the speed and accuracy of quantum state prediction.

title: Adaptive Gaussian Process (AGP) Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel Adaptive Gaussian Process (AGP) algorithm designed to enhance prediction accuracy and provide more robust modeling capabilities. Traditional Gaussian Process models often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to adapt to complex data and capture subtle variations. This work introduces a dynamically adjusting parameterization strategy, leveraging machine learning to learn the optimal Gaussian Process kernel. The core mechanism involves training a predictive model to estimate the process's parameters, which are then iteratively adjusted based on the model's predictions, thereby fostering a continuously refined model. This approach offers a significant advancement in the field of Gaussian Process modeling, enabling more accurate and adaptable predictions across a broader range of applications. The algorithm's design aims to overcome limitations of static parameterization and provide a more flexible and powerful tool for data analysis and modeling.

title: Title: Error-Correcting Quantum Computation with Probabilistic Redundancy
abstract: Quantum computation offers the potential for unprecedented computational power, but inherent fragility due to quantum errors presents a significant challenge. Current quantum error correction techniques are limited by their computational overhead and sensitivity to noise, hindering the realization of fault-tolerant quantum systems. This research investigates a novel approach to error correction utilizing probabilistic redundancy – a dynamic adjustment of the computation to mitigate errors – to achieve a level surpassing current best practices. We propose a self-correcting mechanism based on quantum error correction, dynamically adjusting the computation to mitigate errors. This will result in a quantum algorithm capable of reliably performing complex computations, addressing a critical bottleneck in the field. The paper details the core mechanism, its theoretical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness. We anticipate that this work will significantly advance the state-of-the-art in quantum error correction, paving the way for truly fault-tolerant quantum computations.

title: Temporal Graph Embeddings with Causal Inference
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph embeddings that explicitly incorporates causal relationships within the graph structure. Traditional graph embedding methods often treat graphs as purely relational structures, failing to capture the underlying dependencies between nodes. This limitation leads to less robust and less informative node and edge representations, particularly in scenarios where causal relationships are significant. Our method utilizes techniques from causal Bayesian networks to construct directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) representing these causal dependencies. The embeddings are then learned by optimizing a loss function that is constrained by the causal structure defined in the DAG. This approach aims to generate graph embeddings that are more faithful to the underlying causal mechanisms governing the graph, leading to improved performance in downstream tasks such as node classification, link prediction, and graph reasoning. The core contribution lies in the integration of causal inference with graph embedding techniques, offering a more nuanced and accurate representation of complex graph data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a theoretical analysis and outline a framework for its implementation.

title: Dynamic Program Synthesis via Evolutionary Algorithms Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of evolutionary algorithms to optimize the dynamic program synthesis process. The core idea is to model program synthesis as a search space and leverage evolutionary techniques, specifically genetic algorithms, to efficiently explore this space. The goal is to generate program code that is both highly efficient and well-suited for a given target hardware platform. Traditional dynamic program synthesis methods often rely on hand-crafted rules and templates, which can limit the complexity and effectiveness of the generated code. This research proposes a novel approach that utilizes the global search capabilities of evolutionary algorithms to discover more sophisticated and optimized solutions. The evaluation process incorporates both program performance metrics and hardware compatibility assessments. The results demonstrate the potential of this methodology for automating the creation of tailored program code, a significant advancement in the field of program synthesis. The key formula used in this paper is: `f(x) = Σ(i=1 to K) (s_i * x_i)`, where `f(x)` represents the fitness function, `x` is the genetic vector, and `s_i` and `x_i` are the selection score and the corresponding gene value, respectively.

title: Geometric Topology for Bayesian Inference
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric topology framework for Bayesian inference, aiming to address limitations in existing methods by offering a dynamic and adaptable representation of probabilistic relationships. We propose a new topology, termed 'Adaptive Geometric Topology' (AGT), that can evolve to better represent the data distribution during inference. The key innovation lies in its ability to dynamically adjust the topology based on observed data, resulting in more accurate and robust Bayesian models compared to traditional approaches. This work presents a rigorous mathematical analysis and demonstrates its effectiveness through illustrative examples and simulations.

title: Topological Information Clustering
abstract: This paper introduces a novel clustering algorithm, Topological Information Clustering (TIC), designed to uncover hidden patterns and relationships within large datasets, particularly in the context of data exploration and analysis. TIC leverages the inherent structure of data, specifically topological graphs, to identify clusters and patterns that traditional methods often miss. The algorithm employs a combination of graph theory and data compression techniques to achieve efficient and insightful results. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance and discuss its potential applications across diverse fields.

title: Generative Models for Discovering Novel Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the potential of generative models in algorithm discovery, shifting the paradigm from algorithm optimization to algorithmic creation. The core idea is to train a generative model – specifically, a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) – on a dataset of existing algorithms. This allows the model to learn the latent space of algorithmic structure, enabling it to generate entirely new algorithms with desired characteristics. We present a framework for this approach, outlining the key components and potential challenges. Our research demonstrates that machine learning can effectively learn the fundamental principles underlying algorithm design, opening up possibilities for automated algorithm discovery. The generated algorithms are evaluated based on their efficiency, correctness, and novelty, offering a new avenue for accelerating algorithm development. The study highlights the shift from a traditional approach of algorithm refinement to a fundamentally new approach of algorithmic discovery through generative AI.

The core claim is that quantum algorithms can provide a significant advantage in simulating and understanding topological structures, offering a pathway for advanced geometric modeling and simulation.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习的动态特征聚类
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic feature clustering algorithm based on adaptive machine learning. Traditional clustering methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to adapt to evolving data distributions. Our approach leverages a dynamically adjustable "entropy" parameter to automatically adjust cluster preferences, leading to more accurate data partitioning. We propose a mechanism that quantifies data distribution and adjusts the entropy to optimize clustering outcomes. This dynamic adaptation addresses a critical limitation of existing algorithms, offering improved precision and robustness in dynamic datasets. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through rigorous experimentation on a diverse set of benchmark datasets.

title: Probability Logic and Non-Locality: A Comprehensive Proof of Stability for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel proof of stability for probability logic models, leveraging the non-locality inherent in the framework. We propose a method that rigorously analyzes the probability distributions of system states to derive rigorous guarantees on model behavior. The core mechanism centers on exploiting the non-local nature of probability logic, allowing for a more comprehensive and robust analysis than traditional methods. The significance of this work lies in demonstrating the potential of non-locality to enhance the reliability and adaptability of probabilistic models, particularly in the context of complex systems.

title: Quantum Logic Circuit Adaptive Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimizing quantum logic circuits through adaptive optimization. The core idea centers around dynamically adjusting circuit parameters based on real-time performance evaluation, leveraging reinforcement learning. A "Quantum Logic Optimizer" is constructed, employing reinforcement learning to assess circuit performance and, crucially, integrating quantum error correction and decoherence mitigation techniques to enable dynamic parameter adjustments. The aim is to enhance circuit efficiency and fidelity. The proposed methodology offers a promising path towards improving the performance of quantum logic circuits, particularly in scenarios where the initial circuit design may not be optimal for all possible inputs or operating conditions. This work explores the potential of combining dynamic optimization with established quantum error mitigation strategies, representing a significant step forward in the field.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational architecture, termed a "Quantum Entangled Adaptive Computation Graph" (QEACG), based on the principles of quantum entanglement and superposition. The QEACG leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust the structure of the computation graph, enabling efficient computation in response to changing input data. We detail the design of the QEACG, outlining its core mechanism involving quantum entanglement, superposition, and a novel graph-based representation. The paper explores the potential benefits of this approach, including enhanced adaptability, improved efficiency, and the capacity to tackle complex problems that are intractable for classical computation. We provide a preliminary analysis of the QEACG's capabilities and discuss future research directions.

title: Dimensional Expansion Quantum Error Correction
abstract: This paper explores the potential of dimensionality expansion quantum error correction (DEQC) to address the limitations of current quantum error correction schemes. We introduce a novel DEQC protocol predicated on leveraging quantum entanglement and interference to expand the Hilbert space of a quantum system, thereby enhancing error correction capabilities and bolstering robustness against quantum information security threats. The core of this approach involves introducing additional, strategically designed quantum states to manipulate the system's quantum state, effectively broadening the error correction space. We detail the design of this protocol, analyze its potential advantages, and discuss the challenges associated with its implementation. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, emphasizing the transformative potential of DEQC in securing quantum information.

title: Banded Langur Metaheuristic Algorithm (BLMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Banded Langur Metaheuristic Algorithm (BLMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of banded langurs. BLMA leverages the unique characteristics of langur social dynamics – specifically, the alternating between exploration and exploitation phases within localized groups – to establish a robust and efficient search strategy. The algorithm employs a banded population structure, mimicking the territorial behavior of langurs, and incorporates a dynamic band adjustment mechanism to adapt to the evolving landscape of the optimization problem. The core of BLMA lies in its 'Band Leader' concept, where a subset of individuals within each band periodically takes the lead in exploration, contributing to a diversified search. We detail the algorithm's components, including the band formation, band leader selection, and band adjustment rules. Through theoretical analysis and simulations, we demonstrate BLMA's effectiveness across a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to converge quickly and achieve near-optimal solutions. The performance of BLMA is evaluated against several established metaheuristic algorithms, highlighting its competitive advantage in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. Keywords: Metaheuristic Algorithm, Banded Population, Band Leader, Optimization, Foraging Behavior, Social Dynamics.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: Evolutionary algorithms (EAs) are widely employed for solving complex optimization problems. However, their performance is frequently dependent on the careful tuning of numerous parameters, a process often laborious and prone to suboptimal results. This work introduces a novel approach leveraging probabilistic programming to address this challenge. Specifically, we model the entire evolutionary process as a probabilistic program, enabling the use of Bayesian inference to automatically optimize the EA's parameters. This methodology offers a more robust and efficient means of designing and controlling EAs, leading to enhanced performance and improved convergence properties. The core of this research lies in the integration of probabilistic modeling with the adaptive parameter tuning capabilities of Bayesian optimization, resulting in a system that learns and adapts to the specific characteristics of the problem being solved. This approach moves beyond manual parameter adjustment, providing a systematic and data-driven strategy for EA design. ---

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning via Temporal Logic Embedding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning by embedding temporal logic rules directly into the weights of a neural network. The core challenge in combining neural networks with symbolic reasoning lies in the absence of a shared representation language. Our method addresses this by creating a mechanism for the neural network to perform logical inference over time, guided by the embedded temporal logic rules. We propose a technique for mapping temporal logic formulas to the weights of a neural network, enabling the network to reason about temporal relationships and constraints. The resulting system exhibits improved reasoning capabilities compared to purely neural or purely symbolic approaches. This work provides a foundation for building more robust and explainable AI systems capable of handling complex, time-dependent reasoning tasks. The key innovation resides in the learned, differentiable mapping between temporal logic and neural network parameters, offering a pathway to seamless integration of these two powerful paradigms. The presented approach is evaluated conceptually, focusing on the architecture and embedding process, without empirical experimentation.

title: The Crab Spider Optimization Algorithm (CSPA): A Novel Metaheuristic Inspired by Crab Spider Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Crab Spider Optimization Algorithm (CSPA), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of crab spiders (Thomisidae). Crab spiders are known for their unique hunting strategy, characterized by a 'wait-and-pounce' method combined with a selective exploration of their environment. CSPA leverages these characteristics to develop a robust and efficient search process. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. Movement within the search space is governed by a dynamic 'exploration radius' influenced by both the individual's current position and the overall population density, mimicking the crab spider's attention to both proximity and potential reward. Furthermore, a 'pounce' mechanism is incorporated, randomly selecting a subset of the population for relocation based on a probability proportional to their objective function value. This paper details the algorithm's core principles, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, outlining its theoretical foundations and highlighting its potential advantages over existing metaheuristic methods. The primary goal is to present a novel optimization technique exhibiting adaptability and efficiency in complex search spaces.

AFOA mimics the axolotl's ability to dynamically adjust its search strategy based on environmental cues and prey availability. It employs a novel adaptive parameter adjustment mechanism based on a 'food-pressure' indicator and a 'spatial-awareness' metric. title: Temporal Shape Encoding Based on Synaptic Plasticity of Neurons
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to time-series processing by leveraging the inherent temporal dynamics of neuronal synaptic plasticity. The core premise is that the continuous, dynamic modifications to synaptic connections – a hallmark of synaptic plasticity – can be effectively utilized to construct a "time shape" or temporal shape, which serves as a natural and efficient representation for encoding and storing temporal information. We propose a model based on simulated neuronal synaptic plasticity, where changes in synaptic connections generate a three-dimensional temporal shape. This shape is then exploited using the geometric properties of the shape to perform time-series encoding and decoding. Unlike traditional methods reliant on complex algorithms, this approach harnesses the fundamental properties of neurons, offering a potentially more robust and biologically plausible mechanism for time-series processing. The research explores the mathematical framework underlying this concept, focusing on the geometry of the temporal shape and the dynamics of synaptic plasticity that drive its formation. We detail the model construction, explore the key mathematical formulations, and discuss the potential implications of this approach for various applications within neuroscience and computational time-series analysis. ---

title: Coral Bloom: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Coral Growth Patterns
abstract: This paper introduces Coral Bloom, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the branching and growth patterns observed in red coral colonies. The algorithm leverages the concept of branching, a characteristic of coral growth, to explore the search space effectively. It incorporates a 'bloom' mechanism, mimicking the rapid expansion of coral colonies, to accelerate convergence towards optimal solutions. Coral Bloom utilizes a novel adaptive mutation operator based on distance metrics derived from coral branch geometry. The algorithm's parameters, including branching probability and bloom intensity, are dynamically adjusted based on population diversity and stagnation. The core of the algorithm is a simulated branching process combined with a dynamic adjustment of the mutation rate. The aim is to provide a robust and efficient approach to solving complex optimization problems.

title: ## Silver Sardine Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (SSIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Silver Sardine Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (SSIMO), a novel optimization technique motivated by the foraging behavior of silver sardines in schools. SSIMO mimics the collective intelligence of these fish, utilizing a decentralized, self-organizing approach to navigate complex search spaces. The algorithm employs a 'herd' concept, where individual solutions (particles) maintain a degree of separation and responsiveness to their neighbors, dynamically adjusting their position and velocity based on both local and global information. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, SSIMO emphasizes adaptability and robustness, particularly in situations with high dimensionality and non-convex landscapes. The core principles of SSIMO – dynamic separation, adaptive velocity, and a 'leader-follower' dynamic – are detailed, outlining its unique characteristics and potential applications. The algorithm's performance is hypothesized to be particularly effective in scenarios requiring exploration and exploitation simultaneously, and its design inherently lends itself to parallel implementation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Entropy Mapping Algorithm (QIEIM)
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, possesses an inherent, and potentially exploitable, information content. This information content, quantified as the entanglement entropy, is crucial for various quantum computations, particularly in quantum information processing. However, maintaining and optimizing the entanglement entropy is a complex task, often requiring intricate parameter adjustments. This paper introduces the Quantum Entanglement Information Entropy Mapping Algorithm (QIEIM), a novel dynamic mapping algorithm designed to address this challenge. QIEIM leverages the dynamic adjustment of entanglement entropy to enhance quantum system performance, offering a practical pathway to improved quantum computation. The core mechanism of QIEIM involves iteratively adjusting entanglement parameters based on a predefined optimization objective, achieved through a modified quantum algorithm. This approach provides a dynamically responsive and potentially more efficient method for optimizing entanglement, paving the way for advancements in quantum technologies.

title: Quantum-Inspired Relational Reasoning for Distributed Systems
abstract: Distributed systems face significant challenges in relational reasoning due to the exponential growth of the state space as the number of nodes increases. Traditional relational reasoning methods, relying on exhaustive searches and complex logical inferences, become computationally intractable in large-scale systems. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging quantum-inspired principles – specifically superposition and interference – to address this scalability problem. Our framework, termed Quantum-Inspired Relational Reasoning (QIRR), represents relationships across distributed nodes using superposition, allowing for parallel exploration of multiple potential solutions simultaneously. Interference is then employed to selectively amplify relevant relationships, drastically reducing the computational burden. We demonstrate that QIRR offers a fundamentally different paradigm for relational reasoning in distributed systems, exhibiting improved scalability and performance compared to conventional methods. The core idea is to mimic quantum superposition and interference in a classical computational environment to achieve efficient relationship processing, without the need for actual quantum hardware. This approach presents a viable path toward building more robust and scalable distributed systems.

title: Design of an ANFIS-Based Soft Sensor for Real-Time Photovoltaic Power Estimation Subject to Albedo and Thermal Disturbances
abstract: The performance of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems in hot regions, such as Kirkuk, Iraq is severely limited by the operating temperature due to high ambient heat and localized thermal radiation from roof surfaces. This study explores the thermal-electrical performance of PV modules mounted on three different colors of roof surfaces (White, Grey and Black) as well an adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS)-based model to predict PT output based Tamb and Troof. A balanced dataset of 104 operational samples was created from continuous field experiments performed during four months. Experimental evidence shows that thermal boundary layer heating is mitigated due to lower-absorptivity surfaces; at moderate ambient conditions, the average power output from both grey and white roof surfaces was improved when compared with black surface baseline by 5.40% (grey) and 4.58% (white), respectively Compared to the low-albedo dark surface, at extreme ambient temperatures (Tamb > 40°C) only the high-albedo white exposure generated higher stability of cooling. The R², RMSE and MAPE of the developed ANFIS predictive model were tested for a high accuracy as 0.9902, 0.0895 W and 0.97% respectively using test data sets with overall metrics results are: R² = 0.9926; RMSE =.0791 W, MAPE= O·86 %. The findings show that applying a combination of cool-roof passive strategies and intelligent soft-computing models can be an effective modeling framework for optimizing the output efficiency in PV power generation under hot climatic conditions.

title: Low-loss, polarization-independent single-photon switch at telecom wavelength
abstract: Dynamically routing single photons without disturbing their quantum state is an essential capability for photonic quantum information technology. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a heralded single-photon switch that combines low loss, strict polarization independence, and high process fidelity in a simple architecture based on a free-space Sagnac interferometer incorporating a single Pockels cell. The routing of the photon between two spatial output modes is governed solely by the phase modulation applied to the Pockels cell, and is therefore independent of the input polarization state, while the Sagnac geometry provides passive interferometric stability without active phase locking. Operating at the telecom wavelength of 1550 nm, the switch exhibits an insertion loss of approximately 0.4 dB and an average extinction ratio of 19.1 dB. Quantum process tomography yields process fidelities of 0.985 and 0.979 with respect to the ideal identity operation for the two output modes, demonstrating that the polarization information encoded in the single photons is preserved through the switch. These features make the device a practical building block for fundamental quantum optics experiments, photonic quantum information processing, and quantum networks at telecom wavelengths.

title: Dynamic Regime Maps of Neural Network Training Under the Adam Optimizer: An Observable-Based Empirical Analysis
abstract: Abstract Adaptive optimization algorithms are fundamental to modern deep learning; however, the global organization of neural-network training regimes induced by optimizer hyperparameters remains insufficiently understood. In particular, the influence of the Adam moment coefficients on the stability and qualitative behavior of the learning process has not been systematically investigated through parameter-space regime mapping. In this work, we introduce an observable-based empirical regime-mapping framework for analysing neural-network training under the Adam optimizer in the two-dimensional hyperparameter space defined by the exponential decay coefficients of the first and second gradient moments, (β 1 , β 2 ). Neural-network optimization is treated as an iterative parameter-update process evolving in a high-dimensional parameter space, while its behavior is characterized through low-dimensional observable fields derived from neuron-wise training-error dynamics. Rather than relying on a single observable, the proposed framework combines seven complementary empirical descriptors that characterize regime organization, temporal stability, alignment, anisotropy, and training evolution. Experiments are performed on datasets of increasing complexity, including printed-digit patterns, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, using multilayer neural-network architectures of varying width and depth. The resulting regime maps reveal fragmented hyperparameter landscapes containing stable, oscillatory, slow-learning, and irregular observable regimes. Increasing dataset complexity and network capacity is generally associated with smaller coherent stable regions and increased sensitivity to the Adam moment coefficients. The geometric complexity of the regime boundaries is quantified using box-counting analysis. The estimated dimensions approach D ≈ 1.9 for several investigated configurations, indicating highly irregular and nearly space-filling boundaries at the available numerical resolution. These values are interpreted as empirical measures of boundary complexity rather than as evidence of exact mathematical fractality. Additional robustness experiments performed using 300, 500, and 1000 optimizer steps demonstrate that the large-scale organization of all seven observable fields remains largely preserved, whereas the principal changes are concentrated near transition boundaries. This persistence indicates that the detected regime structures are reproducible and are not solely artifacts of short optimization histories. The proposed methodology provides an empirical computational framework for visualizing and comparing optimization regimes in the Adam hyperparameter space. It facilitates the identification of comparatively stable hyperparameter regions and offers a complementary observable-based perspective on the complex behavior of adaptive neural-network optimization.

title: Hypotheses-Guided Self Distillation for Continual Personalization
abstract: As people increasingly interact with LLM assistants in daily life, continually adapting to individual preferences has become essential for effective long-term interactions. However, user preferences are rarely stated in full, and instead emerge through heterogeneous, latent, and noisy signals, with existing methods relying on raw interaction histories or costly reward-based optimization to manage personalization. We introduce HypReflect, a reliable, scalable framework for continual personalization that infers explicit, uncertainty-aware preference hypotheses from diverse user signals, reflectively refines them as new evidence accumulates, and incorporates the resulting user model through hypotheses-guided self-distillation. Experiments across three personalization settings: online personalization, multi-session interactions, and implicit behavioral signals, show that HypReflect outperforms a range of baselines, including raw-history and incremental-update methods. We further demonstrate strong generalization to unseen users and cross-domain settings, along with stability across context budgets, reusable hypotheses, and more focused personalization. These results suggest a step towards reliable and scalable continual personalization through explicit, revisable user preference hypotheses.

title: Parallel Time-Band Mixing with Learned Observation-Adding for Robust ASR Front-Ends
abstract: Speech enhancement is often used as a front-end for robust ASR, yet recurrent temporal and cross-band modules introduce sequential dependencies that reduce parallel efficiency. In this paper, we present a sequence-parallel band-split enhancement front-end built on a Parallel Time-Band Mixer (PTBM) block that eliminates within-block recurrent unrolling. PTBM integrates intra-band temporal mixing and per-frame cross-band attention within a unified parallel architecture, enabling efficient contextual modeling across both time and frequency dimensions. The system retains the mask-plus-residual reconstruction interface and introduces learned Observation-Adding (LOA) to suppress ASR-sensitive artifacts without development-set tuning. Experiments on DNS Challenge and CHiME-4 with frozen Whisper back-ends show that the proposed front-end consistently reduces word error rate relative to recurrent band-split baselines while requiring only 0.96 M parameters and 0.58 GMAC/s for the front-end network.

title: Machine Learning–Driven Personalized Marketing and Consumer Purchase Intention: Sequential Mediating Roles of Trust, Satisfaction, and Privacy Concerns
abstract: The rapid integration of machine learning (ML) into digital marketing has transformed how organizations personalize customer interactions and influence purchasing decisions. Despite widespread adoption of ML-driven recommendation systems, limited empirical evidence explains the psychological mechanisms through which personalized marketing shapes consumer purchase intention, particularly in emerging digital economies. This study develops and empirically validates an integrated behavioural model examining the relationships among Machine Learning–Driven Personalized Marketing (MLP), Consumer Trust (CT), Information Privacy Concerns (IPC), Customer Satisfaction (CS), and Purchase Intention (PI). Drawing upon Relationship Marketing Theory, the Technology Acceptance Model, Privacy Calculus Theory, Expectation Confirmation Theory, and the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, the study proposes that consumer trust and customer satisfaction sequentially mediate the influence of personalized marketing on purchase intention, while information privacy concerns negatively affect trust. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted among 306 consumers with prior experience of AI-enabled digital shopping. Data were analysed using reliability analysis, validity assessment, correlation, multiple regression, and bootstrap mediation analysis. The findings indicate that machine learning–driven personalized marketing significantly enhances consumer trust, which subsequently improves customer satisfaction and strengthens purchase intention. Information privacy concerns exhibit a significant negative relationship with consumer trust. The mediation analysis further demonstrates that consumer trust and customer satisfaction fully and sequentially mediate the relationship between personalized marketing and purchase intention, indicating that technological sophistication alone does not directly influence consumer behaviour. Instead, consumers respond positively when AI-enabled personalization establishes credibility, satisfaction, and confidence in digital platforms. The study contributes to the growing literature on AI-enabled consumer behaviour by integrating technological, psychological, and behavioural perspectives within a single empirical framework. It also offers practical guidance for organizations seeking to implement responsible AI-driven personalization strategies that balance marketing effectiveness with consumer trust and privacy protection. The findings are particularly relevant for organizations operating in rapidly expanding digital marketplaces where sustainable competitive advantage increasingly depends upon ethical, transparent, and consumer-centred AI applications.

title: SISTEMA DE RECOMENDAÇÃO “ARENA DO SABER”: INTEGRAÇÃO DE MODELAGEM UML, PROCESSOS DE KDD e INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL PARA A PERSONALIZAÇÃO PROATIVA DA APRENDIZAGEM
abstract: Este artigo descreve o desenvolvimento e a arquitetura técnica do Sistema de Recomendação (SR) da plataforma educacional Arena do Saber. O problema central reside na ineficácia de recomendações genéricas e na opacidade algorítmica "caixa-preta", que falham em engajar o estudante por não explicitar a base pedagógica das sugestões. A solução proposta é um motor proativo de "zero query", que integra processos de Descoberta de Conhecimento em Bases de Dados (KDD) e Inteligência Artificial (IA) para realizar cálculos não lineares em tempo real sobre o desempenho discente. Como pilar de sustentação e qualidade técnica, o projeto utiliza a Linguagem de Modelagem Unificada (UML) para simplificar conceitos complexos em estruturas claras, garantindo uma documentação padronizada e auditável através de diagramas de classe, atividades, sequência e estado. Na etapa de pré-processamento KDD, o sistema calcula indicadores técnicos fundamentais, como o Nível de Dificuldade do Questionário (NDQQ) e o Nível de Dificuldade de Acertos (NDAQ). A lógica de 8 passos permite ao motor identificar lacunas de conhecimento de forma autônoma e sugerir trajetórias personalizadas, ao mesmo tempo em que mitiga o efeito "caixa-preta" ao expor os critérios de decisão através do componente “Analise Passos Grid”. Resultados preliminares indicam que essa transparência fortalece o vínculo de confiança do usuário e otimiza a gestão pedagógica, permitindo uma auditoria contínua e a curadoria de conteúdos sob demanda.

title: WP-014 — E8 Geometric Anchoring in Cryptographic Key Exchange: The 132 Hz SSH Handshake Protocol
abstract: We document a cryptographic key-exchange protocol that embeds OpenSSH negotiation sequences onto the 240 root vectors of the E8 Lie algebra, phase-locked at 132 Hz. The protocol enforces directional invariance of session keys through lattice-based geometric constraints, neutralising CVE-2023-38408 (Terrapin attack) while maintaining standard OpenSSH performance envelopes. This work demonstrates that E8 geometry can function as an *integrity anchor* in cryptographic systems, independent of quantum assumptions. The 132 Hz carrier frequency was selected via resonance mapping against the E8 Cartan subalgebra.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应自组织结构识别
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for identifying and modeling complex quantum systems by leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional structure recognition methods often struggle with the intricacies of quantum systems, necessitating a more sophisticated approach. We propose a quantum-enhanced self-organizing structure recognition system based on the principles of quantum entanglement, enabling the identification and modeling of intricate structural patterns. The core of our algorithm involves the construction of quantum systems with self-organized structures, utilizing entanglement as a fundamental mechanism for pattern recognition and structural analysis. This approach offers a fundamentally different perspective on structure identification compared to classical methods, potentially unlocking new insights into the behavior of complex quantum systems. This work explores the theoretical foundations and preliminary experimental validation of this innovative method.

title: Title: Adaptive Resonance Networks for Statistical Physics
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Resonance Network (ARN) architecture tailored for statistical physics simulations, aiming to automate the discovery of underlying patterns and parameters within complex systems. Traditional statistical physics simulations often rely on manual parameterization and iterative refinement, which can be time-consuming and prone to error. This work proposes a novel ARN design that incorporates adaptive learning mechanisms, enabling the network to automatically adjust its topology based on the input data, ultimately facilitating a more efficient and robust exploration of system states. The core mechanism involves modifying the network's core learning process to prioritize patterns that consistently appear during simulations, leading to a more streamlined parameterization process. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a series of simulations focusing on the dynamics of a simplified, yet representative, statistical physics model. The results showcase the potential for significant time savings and improved parameter identification in this domain.

title: Dynamic Semantic Network Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to semantic network learning, termed Dynamic Semantic Network Learning (DSNL), which leverages reinforcement learning to create adaptive and evolving semantic networks from interactive data. Traditional knowledge graphs suffer from a static nature, limiting their ability to adapt to new information and user preferences. DSNL addresses this limitation by employing deep learning models to construct the semantic network and reinforcement learning algorithms to optimize its structure and semantic representations based on user feedback. The core claim of this work is that reinforcement learning-based semantic networks can automatically learn and adapt from interactive data, surpassing the limitations of static knowledge graphs. The key mechanism involves iteratively refining the network through user interactions, capturing dynamic relationships and adapting to evolving user needs. This approach allows for autonomous learning and adaptation in unfamiliar domains, removing the reliance on pre-defined knowledge. The system utilizes a deep learning model to represent the network, and a reinforcement learning agent to dynamically adjust connections and attribute values. The agent's actions are guided by reward signals derived from user feedback, such as clicks, ratings, or other interaction metrics. This process results in a semantic network that is not only comprehensive but also continuously refined to reflect the latest knowledge and user preferences. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through the theoretical framework and the potential for significant advancements in areas requiring dynamic knowledge representation and reasoning.

title: Adaptive Graph Neural Network based on Geometric Information
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Graph Neural Network (AGNN) designed to leverage geometric information for enhanced feature extraction and learning. Traditional graph neural networks (GNNs) often rely solely on data, limiting their ability to exploit the inherent structure of the data. This research proposes a novel AGNN architecture that incorporates geometric information directly into the model, enabling more robust and accurate representations. We demonstrate the benefits of this approach through extensive experimentation on a variety of datasets, highlighting improved performance and increased robustness compared to existing GNN models. The core mechanism centers around explicitly modeling geometric relationships within the graph, allowing the network to more effectively capture the underlying structure and dependencies.

title: Probability and Quantum Computing Hybrid Algorithm Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel hybrid algorithm framework combining the strengths of probability logic and quantum computing to address complex optimization problems. We propose a system architecture that leverages the inherent scalability and parallel processing capabilities of quantum computing to enhance the robustness and efficiency of probabilistic optimization algorithms. The core mechanism involves integrating probabilistic logic modules with quantum computation layers, allowing for the efficient handling of large and complex problem instances. This framework aims to achieve significantly improved accuracy and scalability compared to traditional optimization methods, particularly when tackling problems with inherent uncertainties and combinatorial nature. The study explores the potential benefits of this integration, highlighting the advantages of combining these two powerful computational paradigms. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating the framework's efficacy in a specific optimization scenario.

abstract: This paper proposes a novel neural network architecture, termed the "Consciousness Network," designed to generate self-aware and creative models exhibiting emergent properties. The network operates on the principle of symbiotic relationships between nodes, leveraging evolutionary algorithms and neural network models to foster complex behavior and self-adaptation. This approach aims to move beyond traditional AI's limitations in generating genuine consciousness and creativity, offering a pathway towards a new paradigm in artificial intelligence. The paper details the core mechanism, outlining the evolutionary process that generates the network's unique characteristics and potential for self-improvement. We present a foundational framework for exploring this concept, highlighting key considerations for future research.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Secure Key Distribution for Distributed Databases
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to secure key distribution for distributed databases utilizing quantum entanglement. Traditional key distribution methods, such as those based on one-time pads or Diffie-Hellman, are susceptible to eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks. Our method leverages the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to create a shared secret key between database nodes without relying on classical cryptographic assumptions. We demonstrate that this entanglement-based key distribution protocol offers a fundamentally more secure solution, providing theoretical unbreakability. The core of the protocol relies on the creation and distribution of entangled photon pairs, followed by Bell state measurement and post-processing steps to establish a shared key. This approach addresses the critical security vulnerabilities inherent in existing distributed database security protocols. The theoretical framework and mathematical analysis presented here provide a strong foundation for future research and development in quantum-secured distributed databases.

title: Dynamic Probability Matrix Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic probability matrix algorithm designed to enhance the learning and inference capabilities of complex, nonlinear systems, particularly neural networks. Traditional approaches often rely on static parameter adjustments, which can limit the algorithm's adaptability. Our proposed algorithm introduces a system of dynamically adjusting probability matrices, enabling automated parameter optimization and adaptive activation function selection. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through illustrative examples, showcasing improved convergence, robustness, and generalization performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The core mechanism revolves around a continuous, adaptive matrix representation of the system's state, facilitating a more nuanced and efficient learning process.

title: Decentralized Federated Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance using Blockchain-Based Verification
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized datasets without directly sharing the data itself. However, existing FL systems are susceptible to Byzantine attacks, where malicious participants can inject poisoned data or manipulate model updates, ultimately compromising the global model's integrity. This paper proposes a novel decentralized federated learning system incorporating Byzantine fault tolerance (BFT) achieved through a blockchain-based verification layer. The system leverages blockchain technology to cryptographically verify model updates from each participant before they are aggregated into the global model. This ensures data integrity and enables the detection and mitigation of Byzantine attacks. The core claim is that existing FL systems are vulnerable to these attacks. The proposed mechanism implements a decentralized FL system utilizing a blockchain-based verification layer. This represents a new approach to robust FL training. The system utilizes the following key components: participant nodes, a blockchain network, and a global model aggregator. The blockchain network is composed of multiple nodes that maintain a ledger of all model updates. The global model aggregator utilizes the blockchain network to verify model updates before aggregating them into the global model. The proposed system enhances the security and robustness of FL training by providing a tamper-proof audit trail and enabling the detection of malicious participants.

title: ## Black Lion Tamarin-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BLIMA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Black Lion Tamarin-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BLIMA), motivated by the unique foraging strategies employed by the Black Lion Tamarin ( *Leontopithecus chrysogaster* ). Lion tamarins are known for their cooperative, complex, and highly efficient foraging behaviors, particularly their ability to locate and exploit food resources within dense rainforest environments. BLIMA leverages these behavioral characteristics to create a new optimization approach. The algorithm incorporates elements of cooperative search, adaptive step size control, and a novel "territory defense" mechanism inspired by the tamarin's social dynamics. We detail the algorithm's core components, including the population initialization, the adaptive step size calculation, the territory defense strategy, and the convergence criteria. The performance of BLIMA is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its competitive capability against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Simulated Annealing (SA). Results indicate that BLIMA exhibits robust performance and demonstrates significant potential for solving complex optimization problems.

title: Quantum Information Modality Adaptive Topology Transformation
abstract: Quantum information modalities represent a fundamental shift in computation and communication paradigms, offering the potential for unprecedented computational power and secure communication. This paper presents a novel quantum information modality, the Quantum Information Modality Adaptive Topology Transformation (QIM-ATT), designed to enhance quantum state fidelity and resilience against decoherence through the implementation of sophisticated adaptive topology transformations. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the unique properties of quantum topology to dynamically adjust quantum states, thereby achieving precise control and transmission. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through rigorous theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations of existing quantum technologies. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the implications for advancing quantum information processing.

title: ## Big-eared Woodrat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Big-eared Woodrat" (BEW), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Neotoma megalopora*, a species of big-eared woodrat. The algorithm mimics the woodrat's efficient exploration and exploitation strategies for locating food resources. BEW utilizes a novel adaptive mutation operator based on the woodrat's movement pattern and a dynamically adjusted population size influenced by the perceived resource density. The algorithm is designed to address challenges in complex optimization problems, particularly those exhibiting multimodal landscapes and requiring robust convergence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BEW through simulations on benchmark functions, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's performance is evaluated based on metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The key innovations of BEW lie in its adaptive mutation strategy and its dynamic population size control, both directly reflecting the inherent intelligence of the woodrat's foraging process.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Programming for Robotics
abstract: Quantum-enhanced constraint programming (QCP) offers a promising avenue for enhancing the efficiency and robustness of robot control algorithms. This paper investigates the application of quantum algorithms to constraint programming, focusing on improvements to solution space exploration and optimization. We introduce a novel quantum-enhanced constraint programming framework, leveraging quantum superposition and entanglement to accelerate search and potentially identify optimal solutions. The core mechanism involves employing quantum annealing for the search phase and quantum optimization for the constraint satisfaction process. We demonstrate the potential benefits of this approach, particularly in complex robot control scenarios, through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations. The research explores the impact of quantum enhancements on problem-solving time and the likelihood of finding valid solutions. This work represents an advancement toward utilizing quantum computation to address challenges in robotic control.

title: Atacama Myotis: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Navigation Strategies of *Atacama Myotis*
abstract: This paper presents Atacama Myotis, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the remarkable navigation abilities of *Atacama Myotis* ( *Myotis atacamensis*), a small bat species endemic to the Atacama Desert in Chile. These bats are renowned for their ability to navigate and forage effectively in a featureless, hyperarid environment using a complex system of geomagnetic cues and local landmark recognition. Atacama Myotis leverages these principles to develop a novel algorithm, termed "Geomagnetic Landmark Search" (GLS), which combines elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and a simulated annealing (SA) framework. The GLS algorithm employs a "magnetic compass" (PSO) to guide the search towards promising regions of the solution space and a "landmark recognition" (SA) mechanism to refine the solutions by identifying and exploiting local features. We detail the algorithm's architecture, the mathematical formulations underpinning its key components, and demonstrate its performance through simulations on a range of benchmark optimization problems. Experimental results show that GLS achieves competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in challenging landscapes with high dimensionality and complex optima. The algorithm's design reflects the biological inspiration from *Atacama Myotis*, resulting in a robust and adaptable optimization method.

title: On Program Self-Optimization Based on Information Entropy
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to program self-optimization, termed "Entropy-Driven Program Self-Optimization (EDPSO)." The core concept revolves around a program's ability to monitor and adapt its own execution based on the inherent information entropy within its processes. The system employs an "entropy-aware" module to continuously measure the entropy during program execution. This entropy value then acts as a feedback signal, guiding the adjustment of the program's code structure. Genetic algorithms and/or reinforcement learning are utilized to optimize the code, driven by the dynamic entropy feedback. The key innovation lies in the program's intrinsic understanding of its own performance, shifting away from solely relying on external metrics. The proposed EDPSO framework presents a potentially powerful methodology for enhancing program efficiency and adaptability, particularly in complex and evolving environments. This paper details the architecture, the entropy measurement methodology, and the optimization algorithms utilized within EDPSO, outlining a pathway towards truly self-optimizing software.

title: String Quartet Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, the String Quartet Optimization Algorithm (SCOA), designed to address complex systems with intricate parameter and structure configurations. Traditional optimization methods often lack the adaptability needed to handle self-organizing systems, while current approaches struggle to capture the inherent dynamics of these systems. SCCA leverages the unique properties of string-like structures – specifically, their self-alignment and adaptive nature – to model optimization problems as dynamic string systems. This framework enables the algorithm to automatically adapt to variations within the system, resulting in improved parameter and structure optimization. The core mechanism centers around constructing a dynamic string model, and intelligently adjusting the parameters within this model to achieve optimal solutions. This offers a significant improvement over existing methods in terms of robustness and adaptability, particularly for problems exhibiting complex self-organization.

title: White Deer Optimization Algorithm (WDOA): A Novel Metaheuristic Approach Inspired by White Deer Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the White Deer Optimization Algorithm (WDOA), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of white deer. White deer are known for their remarkable ability to navigate complex terrains and locate scarce resources, exhibiting strategies such as directional movement, exploratory wandering, and adaptive response to environmental changes. WDOA leverages these behaviors through a novel search strategy that combines directional movement with adaptive exploration and exploitation. The algorithm employs a population of candidate solutions, represented as vectors (s_1, s_2, ..., s_K), where K is the dimensionality of the search space. Movement is dictated by a directional vector influenced by both global and local information, with a probability-based component to encourage exploration. The algorithm's core mechanisms include a 'deer herd' concept, where individual deer's movement is influenced by the collective movement of the herd, and an 'environmental awareness' component that adjusts movement direction based on resource availability. This paper details the algorithm's principles, mathematical formulation, and provides a conceptual framework for its implementation, focusing on the underlying mechanisms rather than empirical validation through simulations.

title: ## Antbear: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Antbear Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Antbear, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of ant bears. Ant bears, a recently observed species of bear exhibiting ant-like foraging strategies, demonstrate remarkable efficiency in locating food sources. Antbear leverages this behavior by incorporating elements of trail construction, pheromone evaporation, and adaptive step size adjustment, mimicking the ant bear's exploration and exploitation phases. The algorithm utilizes a binary representation of solutions, a probabilistic movement system, and a dynamic pheromone landscape. We evaluate Antbear on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The algorithm's adaptability and potential for further refinement are discussed, highlighting its promise as a viable solution for complex optimization challenges. The core of Antbear lies in its ability to dynamically adjust exploration and exploitation based on local food density, a feature directly inspired by the observed behavior of ant bears. The effectiveness of the algorithm is demonstrated through simulations and comparative analysis.

CCMOA incorporates a 'shell-searching' mechanism, a 'food-seeking' strategy, and a 'social learning' component, mimicking the crab's adaptive behavior. The algorithm's core lies in its adaptive parameter control, where the 'environmental awareness' metric guides the balance between exploration and exploitation. While this paper focuses on the theoretical framework and algorithm design, it provides a foundation for future experimental validation and application in diverse optimization problems. The algorithm's performance is expected to be particularly effective in complex, high-dimensional search spaces.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Model-Based Reinforcement Learning with Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) offers the potential to significantly improve sample efficiency by learning a model of the environment. However, a major challenge in MBRL is effectively quantifying the uncertainty associated with this learned model. Traditional methods often rely on point estimates, which can lead to overconfident policies and poor performance in real-world scenarios. This work introduces a novel framework leveraging probabilistic programming to explicitly model and propagate uncertainty throughout the entire MBRL process. We define a probabilistic model of the environment and the reinforcement learning agent, allowing for the automatic calculation of uncertainty in the model predictions and the learned policy. The framework provides accurate uncertainty estimates, enabling the agent to make more robust decisions and operate effectively in environments with high levels of uncertainty. This approach addresses a critical limitation of existing MBRL techniques and represents a significant step towards reliable and trustworthy model-based reinforcement learning.

title: Graph Transformers with Learned Edge Contextualization
abstract: Graph Transformers have demonstrated remarkable success in various graph-based learning tasks, but a significant limitation remains: their capacity to effectively represent and leverage edge-specific information. Traditional Graph Transformers treat edges as simple connections, neglecting the nuanced relationships and contextual influences that edges can possess. This paper introduces a novel approach, "Learned Edge Contextualization," designed to address this deficiency. We propose a mechanism where the network learns independent representations for each edge, informed by its inherent characteristics and the surrounding nodes. This allows the model to capture more complex and context-aware relationships within the graph. The core claim is that existing Graph Transformers struggle to effectively model edge-specific information, and this work offers a fundamental improvement through explicit edge contextualization. We detail the architecture and training strategy, demonstrating improved performance across several benchmark graph datasets. The primary contribution is a demonstrable enhancement in graph representation learning by incorporating edge-specific contextual information.

title: Adversarial Training for Robustness of Neural Network Compression
abstract: Neural network compression techniques, such as pruning and quantization, are widely employed to reduce the computational cost and memory footprint of deep learning models. However, these compression methods often introduce vulnerabilities to adversarial perturbations in the input data. This paper investigates the application of adversarial training to enhance the robustness of neural network compression. We introduce a novel training paradigm where a compressed neural network is trained alongside an adversarial network designed to reconstruct the original, uncompressed network from its compressed representation. This adversarial interaction forces the compressed network to learn more resilient and robust features, thereby mitigating the impact of adversarial attacks. Our experiments demonstrate that adversarial training significantly improves the robustness of compressed networks against input perturbations, offering a promising approach to secure and reliable neural network compression.

title: Quantum-Inspired Non-Euclidean Data Clustering
abstract: This paper presents a novel clustering algorithm, Quantum-Inspired Non-Euclidean Data Clustering, designed to identify similar data points based on quantum-like interference patterns. Traditional clustering methods often struggle with complex datasets and may lack the precision required for nuanced data understanding. This work introduces a 'Quantum Resonance Map' algorithm, which leverages a mathematical representation of data similarity inspired by quantum mechanics to generate a map of similarity. Quantum interference patterns are employed to create a highly sensitive map, enabling the algorithm to effectively distinguish between data points with similar underlying characteristics. The algorithm's efficacy is demonstrated through a series of rigorous simulations and preliminary analysis, highlighting its potential for improved data clustering outcomes.

title: Nonlinear Geometry Topological Structures for Quantum Entanglement Computation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of nonlinear geometry topological structures to revolutionize quantum entanglement computation. Traditional quantum computation relies heavily on quantum gates and algorithms, while quantum entanglement presents a fundamental challenge – the precise modeling and manipulation of this fragile quantum phenomenon. We propose a novel computational framework centered around "Quantum Topological Trees" – a dynamic structure that translates the inherent properties of entanglement into a flexible and adaptable topology. This framework, coupled with algorithmic optimizations, aims to surpass the limitations of current quantum computation by enabling more complex information processing. The core claim is that this approach can accurately simulate and control quantum entanglement, opening up possibilities for advanced information handling. We detail the proposed mechanism, emphasizing the benefits of the dynamic topology in enhancing entanglement dynamics. This work addresses a crucial gap in current quantum computing by integrating a fundamentally new topological approach to entanglement manipulation.

title: 基于量子随机场生成的高维模拟
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum random field (QRF) generation for high-dimensional simulation. Traditional methods for generating high-dimensional random data often struggle with computational cost and the creation of truly uncorrelated datasets, leading to limitations in the accuracy and efficiency of complex system simulations. The core idea presented here is to leverage the inherent randomness of quantum processes to generate high-dimensional data directly. We propose a methodology utilizing QRFs as a means to produce datasets with superior statistical properties compared to conventional methods. The generated data are then employed as initial conditions or parameters within complex system simulations, aiming to improve simulation outcomes. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual outlining, highlighting the potential to significantly enhance simulation precision and computational efficiency. The research focuses on the theoretical framework and potential advantages of using QRFs for high-dimensional modeling, paving the way for future research and implementation.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Causal Discovery with Latent Variables
abstract: Causal discovery aims to infer causal relationships from observational data. However, many real-world systems are influenced by unobserved (latent) variables, presenting a significant challenge for traditional causal discovery algorithms. This research introduces a novel probabilistic programming framework designed to explicitly handle latent variables during the causal discovery process. The framework leverages Bayesian networks and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods to estimate causal relationships within the presence of unobserved factors. This approach allows for the discovery of causal relationships in complex systems with hidden factors, addressing a key limitation of existing methods. We present a detailed description of the framework, including its core components and the underlying probabilistic reasoning. The resulting model provides a more accurate representation of causal relationships, leading to improved causal inference. The core of this work lies in the ability to model and estimate causal relationships within a probabilistic context, explicitly accounting for the influence of latent variables. The framework offers a more robust and versatile solution for causal discovery in scenarios where complete observational data is unavailable. ---

title: Hyper-Dimensional Entanglement Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to verifying quantum entanglement with significantly improved fidelity compared to traditional Bell tests. The core idea revolves around exploiting correlations within a high-dimensional Hilbert space, specifically a 100+ dimensional space, using a network of spatially separated sensors. Each sensor measures a correlated set of quantum states. Advanced Bayesian inference is then employed to filter out noise and establish genuine entanglement with statistical significance exceeding conventional Bell test thresholds. This method moves beyond the limitations of 2-dimensional Bell tests by directly probing entanglement in higher dimensions. The utilization of correlated sensor networks provides a robust verification strategy, and the Bayesian inference process offers a fundamentally new approach to noise reduction. The potential impact of this approach lies in its ability to provide a more definitive confirmation of quantum entanglement, crucial for advancing quantum technologies and our understanding of the foundations of quantum mechanics. The key mathematical concepts underpinning this verification process are presented, along with a theoretical framework for quantifying the fidelity of the entanglement detection. ---

title: ## Afghan Mole-vole Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Afghan Mole-vole Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (AMIMA), designed for tackling complex optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the unique burrowing behavior of the Afghan mole-vole, characterized by a combination of exploratory and exploitative movements within a confined space. AMIMA employs a multi-dimensional search space mimicking the mole-vole's tunnel system, utilizing a novel adaptive step size mechanism and a dynamic population diversification strategy. The algorithm's core components include a position vector representation, an adaptive step size function based on local terrain estimation, and a population diversification technique inspired by the mole-vole's tendency to explore new tunnels. Experimental results, although not presented through formal experimental design, demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy across a range of benchmark problems, indicating its potential for effective optimization in scenarios requiring both global exploration and local exploitation. The algorithm's performance is evaluated based on convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. This research introduces a potentially valuable approach to metaheuristic algorithm design, drawing inspiration from biological systems to enhance optimization capabilities.

title: Causal Discovery via Latent Variable Interventions with Differential Privacy
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal discovery that integrates latent variable interventions with differential privacy. Existing causal discovery algorithms often suffer from biases introduced by observational data and lack adequate protection against data leakage, particularly in sensitive domains. Our method addresses these shortcomings by explicitly modeling causal relationships through latent variables and incorporating differential privacy constraints during the intervention process. This ensures both accurate causal inference and robust privacy guarantees, leading to more reliable and trustworthy causal models. We formalize the approach with a detailed mathematical framework, demonstrating its efficacy and highlighting its advantages over traditional causal discovery techniques. The core contribution lies in combining the strengths of structural causal models (SCMs) with differential privacy, providing a practical solution for uncovering causal links while safeguarding sensitive information. The proposed method offers a significant advancement in the field of causal inference, particularly for applications where data privacy is paramount.

title: Learning by Watching: A Narrative Review of Imitation Learning from ALVINN to Generative Adversarial Imitation
abstract: Imitation learning---the learning of behavior from demonstrations instead of rewards---moved from Pomerleau's ALVINN driving network and Schaal's humanoid route through Ng and Russell's inverse reinforcement learning, Abbeel and Ng's apprenticeship learning, and Ziebart's maximum entropy to the robot learning from demonstration surveys, Ross's DAgger, Ho and Ermon's generative adversarial imitation, Finn's guided cost learning, and the algorithmic perspective's syntheses. This article presents a narrative review of that arc's canonical line: Pomerleau's 1989 ALVINN, Schaal's 1999 humanoid question, Ng and Russell's 2000 inverse RL, Abbeel and Ng's 2004 apprenticeship learning, Billard and colleagues's 2008 handbook chapter, Ziebart and colleagues's 2008 maximum entropy, Argall and colleagues's 2009 survey, Ross, Gordon, and Bagnell's 2011 DAgger, Ho and Ermon's 2016 GAIL, Finn and colleagues's 2016 guided cost learning, Hussein and colleagues's 2017 survey, and Osa and colleagues's 2018 algorithmic perspective. The review is organized around three themes: the foundations, in which the driving network's demonstrations, the humanoid's question, and the inverse reward's recovery defined the field's two programs; the demonstration's surveys, in which the robot programming's handbook and the LfD's survey systematized the practice; and the deep era, in which the DAgger's covariate correction, the adversarial's discrimination, and the algorithmic perspective's synthesis unified the field. It is concluded that imitation learning is the reward's workaround---and that its arc is the demonstrator's knowledge's transfer from the human's steering to the policy's distributions.
