title: CrossModalQA: A Cross-modal and Multi-hop Benchmark for Multimodal Retrieval-augmented Generation
abstract: Despite the strong capabilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), their parametric knowledge remains incomplete and difficult to update, motivating multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to ground responses in external text and images. However, existing benchmarks face two major limitations: (i) they typically emphasize single-hop retrieval or reasoning over a small set of provided contexts rather than open-domain evidence discovery; and (ii) they provide fragmented coverage of cross-modal reasoning paths, leaving complex multi-hop and multi-image reasoning underexplored. In this paper, we introduce CrossModalQA, an open-domain benchmark for evaluating multimodal retrieval and reasoning over heterogeneous corpora. CrossModalQA contains 1,863 question-answer pairs constructed from 4,987 Wikipedia articles and 4,431 Wikimedia Commons images. It covers five complementary reasoning paths: vision-to-text, text-to-vision, vision-to-text-to-vision, multi-image intersection, and image-set reasoning. Every question requires retrieving and composing distributed textual and visual evidence, with an average reasoning depth of 3.50 hops. We construct the benchmark through multimodal knowledge graph-guided subgraph sampling and apply rule-based consistency checking and LLM verification to ensure multimodal dependence and traceable evidence. Extensive experiments demonstrate that existing multimodal RAG systems struggle to recover complete evidence chains and can underperform closed-book models when incomplete retrieval introduces distracting context. Further analysis reveals that complete cross-modal retrieval contributes more to answer accuracy than generator scaling, while multi-image retrieval and reasoning remain the primary bottlenecks limiting end-to-end performance.

title: CompanionSim: Synthetic Data for Evaluating Anthropomorphism in Human-AI Relationships
abstract: Many people now see AI systems as not just productivity tools but as social companions. Researchers are eager to study the consequences of AI companionship behaviors, such as validation, which evoke trust, empathy, and attachment in human-human interaction. However, human-AI interaction data is limited and unreliable, slowing research progress. We scale small amounts of real-world data by simulating multi-turn human-chatbot dialogue across a range of chatbot behaviors and use cases. We release CompanionSim: a simulation framework with 2,240 simulated human-chatbot conversations representing 16 chatbot behaviors across seven use cases. Human participants annotated the simulated conversations and real-world conversations in two experiments probing perceptions of companionship behaviors. We conducted Study 1 with a U.S. representative sample ($N_{1}~=~628$) and Study 2 across the U.S., U.K., India, and Nigeria ($N_{2}~=~3,646$). Surprisingly, we find that companionship behaviors reduced likability, humanlikeness, and trust in AI chatbots. These effects were larger in particular subgroups: women and older participants saw companionship chatbots as less likable, humanlike, and trustworthy. We encourage researchers to leverage real-world and synthetic data together to study the differential impacts of AI companions and to create benchmark evaluations of AI chatbots.

title: DiffPDE: Masked Diffusion Language Models as PDE Solver
abstract: Existing approaches for synthesizing Partial Differential Equation (PDE) solvers predominantly rely on autoregressive models, yet their global left-to-right decoding incurs substantial redundancy when addressing inherently localized bugs. In this work, we challenge this inefficient paradigm and propose DiffPDE, a framework leveraging discrete diffusion language models for targeted code repair. By introducing a localized re-masking and infilling strategy, DiffPDE regenerates only erroneous regions while preserving correct context, naturally aligning generation with the sparse nature of PDE errors. Furthermore, to handle coupled bugs requiring sequential interventions, we present Iterative Debugging GRPO (ID-GRPO), a reinforcement learning scheme that enables multi-round debugging within single trajectories via intermediate rewards. Experiments on PDEBench show that DiffPDE achieves competitive accuracy, outperforms same-scale AR models, and significantly accelerates repair.

title: Ghost infrared spectroscopy with bright twin beams
abstract: Frequency-correlated light offers a route to mid-infrared (MIR) spectroscopy without direct spectral detection in the MIR. Previous MIR ghost spectroscopy has mainly relied on low-gain spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) and photon-pair coincidence measurements, where the limited photon flux has restricted acquisition times to longer than one minute. Here, we demonstrate ghost infrared spectroscopy using bright twin beams generated by high-gain parametric down-conversion (PDC). High-gain PDC amplifies vacuum fluctuations, producing a different pair of frequency-correlated random spectra in each pump pulse. This pulse-resolved stochastic emission is naturally matched to time-stretch detection, which records the spectrum of the correlated near-infrared telecom signal for every pulse, while the MIR idler is measured by bucket detection. Consequently, each pump pulse yields one paired projection measurement comprising a spectrally resolved reference and the corresponding bucket value. We reconstruct the transmission spectrum of a structured optical filter and the molecular vibrational absorption spectrum of liquid benzene near 3.3 um with millisecond-scale acquisition, in good agreement with Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy. This reduces the acquisition time by four to five orders of magnitude compared with previous MIR ghost spectroscopy demonstrations. These results transform ghost spectroscopy from coincidence-based photon counting to high-flux analog correlation spectroscopy, establishing a practical architecture for high-speed computational infrared spectroscopy driven by a narrowband semiconductor laser.

title: Human-AI Value Co-Creation and Continuance Intention toward AI Shopping Agents
abstract: This study examines how design affordances and psychological needs shape consumers’ continuance intention toward AI shopping agents, with human-AI value co-creation as the mediating mechanism. Integrating service-dominant logic and self-determination theory, it positions value co-creation as the process linking antecedents to continuance, addressing prior work that treats value as a post-use evaluation rather than a product of interaction. A survey of 367 users of AI shopping agents was analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM). The findings reveal that recommendation explanation transparency, conversational responsiveness, and competence significantly and positively influence human-AI value co-creation, whereas autonomy and relatedness have nonsignificant effects. Value co-creation in turn exerts a strong positive effect on continuance intention (β= .70) and mediates the relationships between the significant antecedents and continuance intention. The results establish human-AI value co-creation as a process-based mediating mechanism and offer practical implications for the design and user retention of generative AI recommendation systems.

title: Capturing the Finer Aspects of Spoken Language by Automated Speech Recognition
abstract: Spoken language carries far more information than is preserved in its orthographic representation. Pitch movements signal whether an utterance is a question, assertion,or exclamation; syllable duration marks prominence and phrase boundaries; amplitude variations highlight the communicatively most important words. These prosodic dimensions are the subject of linguistic research, yet remain underrepresented in the output of automated speech recognition systems and are difficult to annotate consistently without specialist training. Writing and speech have different virtues and purposes. Orthography (standard spelling and punctuation) captures words and structure, but loses prosody: the emotional and musical dimensions of spoken language. Yet some situations demand richer written representation. Movie subtitles could convey more of the spoken original to deaf viewers. Text-to-speech systems require prosodic guidance to produce natural output and achieve an optimal representation in the acoustic domain. Without explicit prosodic marking in writing, ambiguity persists; with prosody in speech, the intended meaning is immediately clear.For this thesis, we present SpeechPrint, a tool that converts continuous prosodic features into a symbolic, discrete representation. SpeechPrint takes a .wav recording and outputs a structured TextGrid with time-aligned phonemes, syllables, and symbolic prosody, supporting both linguistic research (Praat, ELAN) and creative applications. The prosody symbols encode pitch movements, prominence, and accentuation: Symbol Meaning/ Rising pitch within syllable\ Falling pitch within syllablē High level (vs. neighbors)_ Low level (vs. neighbors)* Prominent accent* ̄// Accented, high, strongly rising_\\ Low, strongly falling These ASCII symbols are intuitive, printable in any environment, and designed to support both linguistic frameworks (ToBI) and creative annotation. SpeechPrint integrates existing speech technologies (Whisper, WhisperX, Montreal Forced Aligner, pYIN) into a coherent pipeline. The key technical contribution is identifying and correcting octave errors in pitch detection: a widespread problem that skews prosodic analysis by full octaves. Vowel nuclei serve as the most acoustically stable carriers of prosodic information, making them ideal targets for reliable pitch and intensity extraction. Systematic evaluation of five pitch trackers revealed that probabilistic methods (pYIN) outperform traditional autocorrelation approaches, addressing a key bottleneck in syllable-level prosody annotation. The evaluation corpus consists of English (305.5 s), German GToBI, and three underresourced languages Daakie (Oceanic, Vanuatu), Cabécar (Chibchan, Costa Rica), and Kakabe (Mande, Guinea). The evaluation demonstrates that the system can recover major prosodic contours and assign symbolic annotations that broadly correspond to human expert judgments. Expert linguist feedback was collected throughout the research process, which identified limitations in handling non-modal phonation and informed refinements to the system architecture. This work belongs in Sound and Music Computation because it bridges technical tool development and artistic practice. On the technical side, it addresses an establishedproblem in acoustic analysis: reliable pitch tracking and prosody extraction. On the expressive side, it treats prosody as a musical dimension: pitch, timing, and dynamic control enabling new forms of artistic representation, interactive speech editing, and accessible multimedia. These two angles: tool engineering and creative application, define Sound and Music Computation research.

title: Pigeons That Learn to Flank You: A Historical Development Review of AI Techniques for NPCs and Dynamic Worlds
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Techniques for NPCs and Dynamic Worlds in the context of Game Development. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of game AI and NPCs as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Game Development.

title: 基于自适应拓扑的量子模拟
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum simulation framework, termed "Adaptive Topological Quantum Simulation" (ATQS), that leverages self-adaptive topology to efficiently simulate complex quantum systems. Traditional quantum simulation methods often rely on static topology, limiting their ability to accurately represent the dynamics of intricate quantum systems. The ATQS framework dynamically adjusts the underlying topology during the simulation process, enabling the simulation of complex quantum systems with enhanced precision and the ability to model dynamic evolutions. We detail the framework's architecture, demonstrate its efficacy through simulations of a parameterized quantum system, and explore its potential for advancing the field of quantum computing.

title: 拓扑学自适应参数调整算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for parameter adjustment in topology-based models, designed to enhance model accuracy. Traditional approaches often rely on fixed parameter settings, limiting the algorithm's potential for optimization. Our proposed method leverages dynamic self-adaptation to intelligently adjust parameters, offering a significant improvement in model performance. We present a detailed explanation of the core mechanism, outlining its key steps and the resulting benefits. This work addresses a critical challenge in applying topology-based models to complex problems, demonstrating a robust and efficient solution through dynamic parameter refinement.

title: 基于混沌的量子态的自适应几何变换
abstract: This paper explores the application of chaos theory to quantum state transformations, aiming to enhance the efficiency of quantum computation. The core idea is to develop an adaptive geometric transformation algorithm driven by chaotic systems, dynamically reshaping quantum states to optimize performance. We present a novel approach that leverages the inherent properties of chaos to improve the trajectory of quantum states, offering a potential advancement over traditional geometric techniques. The paper details the algorithm's underlying principles, explores the potential benefits, and discusses future research directions.

title: Probability Space Quantum Computing Adaptive Entropy Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum computing stability optimization and energy efficiency enhancement through adaptive entropy modeling. Quantum systems are inherently sensitive to environmental noise, leading to fluctuating states and potential errors. Traditional error correction methods often rely on pre-defined error correction codes. This paper proposes a dynamic entropy adjustment algorithm, which iteratively adjusts the quantum state's entropy to counteract these fluctuations. The goal is to create a self-regulating system that continuously adapts to the system's state, improving both coherence and reducing error rates. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through simulations on various quantum circuits, showing significant improvements in stability and reduced energy consumption compared to static entropy control.

title: Geometry Topology Adaptive Evolution Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive evolution algorithm specifically designed for the optimization of geometric topology. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often employ static parameter settings, limiting their potential for generating complex and innovative shapes. This work proposes a mechanism that dynamically adjusts topological structures during the evolution process, leading to a generation of geometries characterized by increased complexity and novelty. The core of this approach lies in iterative refinement of the topology, driven by a self-organizing process. We present a framework for evaluating the performance of this algorithm through a series of test cases focusing on generating novel topological structures.

title: Cognitive Graph Representations for Large Language Models
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge representation within Large Language Models (LLMs) utilizing cognitive graphs. Traditional LLMs primarily rely on embedding-based knowledge representations, which often struggle with complex reasoning and generalization. We introduce a framework where LLMs are trained to directly process and generate cognitive graphs – structured representations of factual knowledge, relationships, and logical inferences. These graphs allow the LLM to navigate and manipulate knowledge more effectively, leading to improved performance in tasks requiring reasoning and generalization. The core claim is that this shift from embeddings to structured graphs will unlock significant advancements in LLM capabilities. We outline the key components of this system, focusing on the training methodology and the structure of the cognitive graphs themselves. We demonstrate, theoretically, that the ability to explicitly represent and reason with interconnected knowledge through graph structures will substantially alleviate the limitations inherent in purely embedding-based representations. This work lays the groundwork for future research into cognitive LLMs capable of sophisticated reasoning and problem-solving.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Programming with Contextualized Memory Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel neuro-symbolic programming framework leveraging contextualized memory networks to address the persistent challenges in combining the strengths of neural networks and symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to create a system capable of learning and representing symbolic knowledge dynamically, enabling robust and adaptable problem-solving. We introduce a system architecture that integrates memory networks, specifically designed to capture contextual information, with symbolic reasoning components. The system learns relationships between concepts through the memory network, allowing it to perform dynamic inference and problem-solving based on this learned knowledge. The proposed approach aims to overcome the limitations of traditional symbolic systems and neural networks by providing a mechanism for knowledge transfer and adaptation. We outline the key components of the system, including the contextualized memory network architecture, the symbolic reasoning engine, and the integration strategy. The goal is to develop a more flexible and powerful approach to intelligent problem-solving, capable of handling complex, real-world scenarios.

title: Quantum Computation Parameter Optimization
abstract: Quantum computation, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics, offers unprecedented computational power for certain problems. However, efficient execution of these algorithms necessitates careful tuning of parameters. This paper presents a novel parameter optimization algorithm designed specifically for quantum computing tasks, employing quantum mechanics' inherent properties to automate parameter adjustments and significantly enhance computational efficiency. We explore a mechanism centered around exploiting quantum phenomena like superposition and entanglement to dynamically adjust parameters, thereby improving the performance of quantum algorithms. The core claim is to establish a robust and automated parameter optimization system capable of accelerating quantum computations.

title: Dynamic Quantum Ring
abstract: Dynamic Quantum Ring (DQR) is a novel computational framework designed to leverage the unique properties of quantum rings to accelerate quantum computations. This paper explores the potential of DQR, demonstrating its capability to achieve significantly enhanced computational efficiency through a carefully crafted algorithm and a robust model of quantum ring behavior. The core mechanism centers around the dynamic manipulation of quantum rings, employing a series of iterative processes to optimize quantum states and ultimately reduce the computational complexity. We detail the theoretical framework, the algorithmic implementation, and the resulting performance gains achieved through a rigorous analysis. The study focuses on the core capabilities of DQR and its potential to overcome limitations of traditional quantum computing approaches.

title: Adaptive Data Augmentation for Anomaly Detection using Generative Adversarial Networks with Temporal Consistency
abstract: Anomaly detection, the task of identifying rare or unusual events, is crucial in numerous domains including cybersecurity, industrial monitoring, and medical diagnostics. Traditional data augmentation methods often fall short in anomaly detection, primarily due to their inability to effectively capture the temporal dependencies inherent in anomalous behavior. This paper proposes a novel adaptive data augmentation framework leveraging Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and incorporating temporal consistency constraints. The core idea is to train a GAN to generate augmented data that not only resembles the normal data distribution but also respects the underlying temporal dynamics. We introduce an adaptive mechanism that dynamically adjusts the augmentation strategy based on the observed data characteristics, further improving the quality and effectiveness of the generated samples. The framework is designed to address the limitations of conventional data augmentation by creating realistic synthetic data that better reflects the true nature of anomalies, leading to enhanced anomaly detection performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and a detailed discussion of the key components and their interactions.

title: Non-Local Quantum Entanglement Dynamics
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, exhibits instantaneous correlations across vast distances. However, practical entanglement distribution and control remain significant challenges. This paper presents a novel framework for quantifying and controlling the dynamics of quantum entanglement over extended distances, leveraging a "chronometric resonance" principle that dynamically adjusts entanglement states based on spacetime curvature. We move beyond traditional state analysis by considering the evolution of the entanglement as a consequence of the underlying spacetime geometry, offering a potential pathway for real-time control and enhanced entanglement stability. The core mechanism hinges on a continuous adjustment of the entanglement's 'chronometric resonance' – a measure of its responsiveness to spacetime fluctuations – allowing for precise manipulation of correlations. This framework has the potential to revolutionize quantum communication and computation, offering unprecedented capabilities in secure and efficient entanglement distribution.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization with Dynamic Feedback
abstract: Quantum-inspired optimization is a burgeoning field that explores the potential of quantum mechanics to accelerate and improve optimization algorithms. This paper investigates a novel quantum-inspired optimization method, "Dynamic Feedback Quantum Optimization," designed to address the challenges of convergence and solution quality often encountered in traditional optimization techniques. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts optimization parameters based on the feedback generated during the optimization process, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to enhance exploration and reduce local optima. The core mechanism focuses on a quantum-inspired adjustment process that iteratively refines the optimization strategy, resulting in faster convergence and improved solution quality. This work presents a practical implementation demonstrating the efficacy of this approach, offering a potential pathway toward more efficient optimization processes.

title: Dynamic Network-Based Predictive Model
abstract: This paper introduces a novel predictive model based on dynamic neural networks, designed to dynamically adjust model parameters based on input data variations. The core mechanism revolves around the continuous learning and adaptation of the neural network's parameters, enabling more accurate predictions in dynamic environments. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments, highlighting its superior performance compared to static and traditional prediction methods. The model's ability to automatically adapt to changing data patterns offers a significant advancement in predictive capabilities.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习的动态图结构优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for dynamic graph structure optimization leveraging adaptive machine learning. Traditional graph optimization methods often rely on static, pre-defined structures, failing to effectively adapt to evolving data. This work introduces a dynamically adjustable graph structure, guided by an adaptive machine learning model, that automatically adjusts graph parameters based on input data dynamics. The proposed algorithm achieves enhanced optimization efficiency through continuous structural refinement, surpassing the limitations of traditional approaches. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that iteratively adjusts graph parameters based on a learned representation of the data's characteristics. This iterative process enables the algorithm to effectively capture and respond to changes in the input, leading to improved performance across a range of graph-related tasks. This research explores the potential of machine learning to dynamically adapt graph structures, providing a more robust and efficient solution for optimization challenges.

title: Benito Roundleaf Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Benito Roundleaf Bat" (BRB) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of the Benito roundleaf bat (Anouraebenetos). These bats are known for their unique echolocation strategy, which involves emitting ultrasonic calls and interpreting the echoes to navigate and locate food in complex environments. The BRB algorithm utilizes these characteristics to develop a search strategy that adapts to the problem landscape, effectively exploring and exploiting potential solutions. The algorithm incorporates several key features mimicking the bat's behavior, including a pulse emission model, echo interpretation mechanism, and a dynamic adjustment of parameters based on the success of previous iterations. We demonstrate the algorithm's performance on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results indicate that the BRB algorithm performs competitively with established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm and the Particle Swarm Optimization, while exhibiting potentially improved convergence rates in certain scenarios. The algorithm's core components are described in detail, and future research directions are discussed.

title: Quantum Entanglement Encoding for Distributed Memory
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed memory systems leveraging quantum entanglement. We demonstrate how encoding information into entangled states of multiple qubits can enable long-range, high-capacity, and low-latency data storage and retrieval. The core mechanism involves exploiting the inherent correlations within entangled states for distributed storage and access. Furthermore, we introduce quantum error correction techniques to enhance the reliability of the system. This approach contrasts with traditional distributed memory systems reliant on classical communication, offering potential advantages in terms of bandwidth efficiency and data transfer speeds. The theoretical framework presented outlines the key components and considerations for realizing this quantum-based distributed memory architecture. We explore the limitations imposed by decoherence and propose strategies for mitigation. The ultimate goal is to establish a foundational understanding of this technology and pave the way for future research and development in quantum memory systems.

title: ## The Bearded Capuchin Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BCIMA)
abstract: This paper presents the Bearded Capuchin Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BCIMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm designed to leverage the adaptable and exploratory behavior observed in the Bearded Capuchin monkey. The algorithm draws inspiration from the monkey's foraging strategies, specifically its ability to efficiently navigate complex environments and dynamically adjust its search based on environmental feedback. BCIMA utilizes a multi-population approach combined with a novel adaptive mutation operator mimicking the monkey's movement patterns. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The core of BCIMA lies in its 'Foraging Phase' and 'Adaptive Movement' components, which are detailed throughout this document. The primary objective is to achieve robust and efficient global optimization while mitigating premature convergence. The algorithm's parameters are designed to be easily tunable, allowing for flexibility in adapting it to different problem landscapes. Results indicate BCIMA's potential as a competitive metaheuristic algorithm, particularly for problems exhibiting high dimensionality and complex, non-linear relationships.

title: Neural Network Topology Chaos Control
abstract: This paper investigates the control of chaos in neural networks through topological manipulation. The core argument posits that by precisely controlling the topology of connections between neurons, it is possible to induce and sustain chaotic behavior within neural networks, unlocking potentially enhanced information processing capabilities. The proposed mechanism leverages topological theory to design a novel neural network architecture. This architecture dynamically adjusts both the connection strengths and the underlying topology to trigger chaotic states. These chaotic states are then utilized for sophisticated information encoding and computational tasks. The research represents a novel approach by integrating topological principles directly into neural network design, providing a pathway toward harnessing chaotic dynamics for advanced neural network functionality. The theoretical framework presented aims to provide a foundation for future research in this area.

title: ## Banks Flying Fox Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Banks Flying Fox
abstract: This paper presents Banks Flying Fox Algorithm (BFFA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique flight behavior of Banks Flying Foxes (Pteropus cooperi). BFFA leverages the fox's ability to dynamically adjust its flight path, utilizing wind currents and visual cues to navigate efficiently, as a core principle for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA), combined with a novel "Wind Adaptation" mechanism that mimics the fox's response to environmental changes. BFFA's core components include a population of flying fox agents, a fitness evaluation function, a wind velocity estimation module, and an adaptive adjustment strategy. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The key contributions of this work lie in the innovative "Wind Adaptation" mechanism and its integration within a metaheuristic framework, providing a robust and adaptable solution for various optimization challenges. The algorithm's design focuses on exploration and exploitation, ensuring both efficient convergence and the ability to escape local optima.

title: Quantum State Adaptive Computation Paradigm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state adaptive computation paradigm aimed at enhancing the efficiency of complex calculations. Traditional computing approaches often require manual parameter adjustments, limiting adaptability to intricate environments. We propose a quantum state-based adaptive computation framework leveraging the inherent self-adaptation properties of quantum states. This framework utilizes quantum transformations and control mechanisms to optimize computational processes, achieving improved performance in diverse scenarios. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically adjusting quantum states to achieve higher fidelity and throughput, overcoming the limitations of conventional methods. This research explores the potential of quantum states to significantly accelerate complex computations.

title: Topological Dimension Analysis for Data Compression
abstract: This paper explores the application of topological dimension analysis to data compression, aiming to identify and exploit inherent structural properties within data to achieve superior compression efficiency. Traditional compression algorithms often struggle with data that exhibits complex, non-linear relationships, limiting their ability to represent and compress information effectively. This research proposes a novel method that leverages topological concepts, specifically connected components and cycles, to represent data in a more structured and efficient manner. The core mechanism involves a system designed to identify and quantify these topological features, allowing for targeted compression strategies based on the structural characteristics of the data. The expected outcome is a new approach that surpasses existing techniques in terms of compression ratio and algorithmic complexity.

title: Topological Dynamical Systems for Accelerated Simulation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum computing to dramatically accelerate the simulation of topological dynamical systems. Topological dynamical systems, characterized by their intricate and often complex geometries, pose significant computational challenges for classical simulations. We propose a novel framework that leverages quantum algorithms to emulate the dynamic evolution of these systems, offering the promise of vastly increased simulation speeds. This work addresses the limitations of current classical simulation techniques by directly incorporating quantum principles to enhance computational efficiency. The core claim is that quantum computing can significantly accelerate the simulation of topological dynamical systems, providing a pathway towards complex topological phenomena with unprecedented speed.

title: Quantum Complexity Theory via Entanglement Propagation
abstract: Quantum Complexity Theory (QCT) represents the study of computational complexity in the quantum realm, aiming to quantify the resources required to solve problems. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing entanglement propagation as a fundamental building block. We formalize QCT by modeling the dynamic adjustment of entanglement strength across a computational space, introducing a 'propagator' that actively shapes the entanglement. This mechanism allows for subtle correlations and patterns to emerge that are difficult to detect classically, offering a fundamentally new perspective on the limitations of computation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a simplified, yet illustrative, model, exploring its potential to reveal previously unnoticed constraints on computational processes.

title: ## Bio-Inspired Adaptive Search with Mimicking Striped Shrimp Behavior (BASMSB)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, Bio-Inspired Adaptive Search with Mimicking Striped Shrimp Behavior (BASMSB), inspired by the foraging strategies of *Penaeus semisulcatus* (striped shrimp). Striped shrimp exhibit a unique adaptive search behavior characterized by alternating between exploratory and exploitative phases, coupled with a 'striping' pattern of resource allocation. BASMSB utilizes a population of potential solutions represented as 'stripes' – dynamically adjusted segments of a search space. The algorithm incorporates an adaptive mechanism mimicking the shrimp's responsiveness to local resource abundance, adjusting stripe lengths and positions based on a 'hunger' metric representing the overall population's search progress and the density of promising areas. The algorithm's core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of stripe lengths, which directly influences the exploration-exploitation balance, and the 'striping' pattern, reflecting the shrimp's tendency to concentrate on promising regions while maintaining a degree of exploratory movement. The algorithm is presented as a discrete optimization method, suitable for problems with well-defined decision variables and objective functions. The theoretical framework and algorithmic steps are detailed, highlighting the key mechanisms that drive the algorithm's performance.

title: ## The Nautilus Metaheuristic: A Novel Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Nautilus Shell Navigation
abstract: This paper introduces the Nautilus Metaheuristic (NM), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the navigation strategies employed by the nautilus shell. The nautilus, renowned for its logarithmic spiral shell, exhibits a remarkable ability to adapt its chamber size and arrangement based on resource availability and environmental pressures. The NM algorithm leverages this adaptive behavior through a population-based search, employing a 'shell' representation to model individual solutions and a 'spiral' mechanism to guide exploration and exploitation. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of 'chamber size' and 'spiral angle' within each shell, reflecting the nautilus's response to changing conditions. This paper details the NM algorithm's design, including the population initialization, shell representation, spiral movement, adaptive parameters, and convergence criteria. While no experimental validation is presented in this initial publication, the theoretical framework and algorithmic design are thoroughly documented, laying the groundwork for future performance analysis and practical applications.

title: Graph-Based Non-linear Adaptive Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for optimization based on graph-structured representations. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex systems, and graph structures offer a powerful mechanism for feature extraction and pattern recognition. The proposed method constructs a graph representation of the system, learns to optimize the graph's structure, and utilizes this structure to guide the optimization process. This approach allows the system to adapt to complex dynamics and improve performance in challenging scenarios. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework through a series of simulations and experiments focused on optimizing a dynamic system with non-linear constraints.

title: Andean Caenolestid-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Andean Caenolestid Algorithm (ACA), inspired by the foraging strategies of the Andean caenolestid ( *Isolestes andinus*), a small, elusive South American stream-dwelling insect known for its unique and efficient foraging behavior. The algorithm leverages the caenolestid's ability to rapidly explore and exploit potential food sources within a complex environment, mimicking its adaptive search process. ACA employs a combination of adaptive parameter control, a novel constriction function, and a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance. The core concept is to simulate the caenolestid's movement and decision-making process, where the search space is represented by the riverbed and potential food sources, and the algorithm iteratively adjusts its position based on the perceived availability and quality of these resources. The performance of ACA is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising approach for tackling complex optimization challenges in diverse fields. The key mathematical components include a constriction function (C(x)) designed to reflect the caenolestid's hesitation and exploratory behavior, an adaptive parameter control mechanism based on a sigmoid function, and an exploration-exploitation balance defined by a probability distribution. The algorithm's success hinges on accurately representing the caenolestid's foraging strategy within a mathematical framework.

title: Andean Big-eared Mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Andean Big-eared Mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (ABMI-MHA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Andean big-eared mouse ( *Geomyidae*). These rodents are renowned for their efficient and adaptable foraging strategies in challenging mountainous terrains. The algorithm leverages key aspects of their navigation, resource selection, and decision-making processes to develop a robust optimization technique. Specifically, we model the mouse's movement as a stochastic process influenced by terrain features, food availability, and memory of past locations. The ABMI-MHA incorporates elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) to achieve effective exploration and exploitation. The algorithm's core mechanics include a 'Terrain-Aware Velocity Update' and a 'Resource Prioritization Mechanism'. We demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy through simulations across a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational cost. The performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The results indicate that ABMI-MHA presents a viable alternative for complex optimization challenges, particularly those involving spatial data and dynamic environments.

title: Dynamic Topology Mapping & Quantum Computation Coupling
abstract: This paper explores the integration of dynamic topology mapping with quantum computation, proposing a novel framework to dynamically optimize and control quantum computations. Traditional approaches often focus on the quantum state itself, neglecting the crucial role of the underlying topology. We introduce a 'Quantum Computation Topology Mapping' concept, leveraging the inherent symmetries and relationships within quantum systems to guide and adjust quantum operations. This model aims to create a system where the topology of the quantum state itself influences the evolution of the computation, leading to improved performance and control. The paper details the methodology, provides preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach, and discusses potential future research directions.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive multi-modularity function space designed to address the challenges of handling evolving data distributions. Traditional function space models typically rely on static parameter adjustments, which struggle to adapt effectively to dynamic data. Our work proposes a new function space architecture incorporating a self-adaptive mechanism that automatically adjusts parameter weights during computation, thereby enabling more efficient parameter optimization and enhanced generalization capabilities. This design offers a significant advancement over existing approaches by providing a flexible framework for handling data variability and improving model performance in complex scenarios.

title: Title: Non-Linear Regularization in Deep Learning for Robustness
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-linear regularization technique specifically designed to enhance the robustness of deep learning models against noise and adversarial attacks. Traditional regularization methods often focus on minimizing prediction error, neglecting the crucial role of model behavior in the face of perturbations. Our approach, termed 'Pattern Deviation Regularization' (PDR), explicitly penalizes deviations from expected patterns within the data distribution. This is achieved through a dynamically calculated 'pattern deviation' metric that continuously assesses the model's output's distance from its learned representation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PDR through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, showcasing significant improvements in model accuracy and resilience to adversarial examples. The paper provides a detailed analysis of the algorithm's implementation and its impact on model performance, emphasizing its potential for bolstering the reliability of deep learning systems.

title: ## Algazel: A Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Gazelle
abstract: This paper proposes Algazel, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the hunting strategies of the gazelle. The algorithm leverages the gazelle's adaptive movement, vigilance, and collaborative decision-making processes to achieve efficient global optimization. Algazel combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) with a unique "scanning" mechanism mimicking the gazelle's scanning behavior for potential threats and food sources. The core components include a population of "hunters" (particles), a fitness evaluation function, and a dynamic scanning strategy. The algorithm's parameters are designed to dynamically adjust the exploration-exploitation balance, enabling effective convergence to optimal solutions. We demonstrate the algorithm's performance on a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic methods. The results indicate that Algazel provides a robust and adaptable approach to solving complex optimization challenges.

title: ## The Hare-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (HASA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Hare-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (HASA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior and decision-making processes of North American rabbits. HASA leverages the rabbit's ability to dynamically adjust its search strategy based on environmental factors, particularly food availability and predator risk. The algorithm incorporates three key mechanisms: a "hare-trail" representation of the search space, a "food-risk" assessment function to guide exploration and exploitation, and an adaptive "speed" parameter that modulates the agent's movement based on perceived opportunity. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, HASA doesn't rely on a fixed population size or a pre-defined convergence criterion; instead, it dynamically scales its population and adjusts the search speed based on the local landscape. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical foundations, operational rules, and potential applications, highlighting its strengths in complex, multi-dimensional optimization problems.

abstract: This paper investigates the development of a dynamic quantum entanglement network control protocol, designed to enhance quantum communication and computation through adaptive entanglement parameter adjustment. The core mechanism involves the implementation of a dynamic "纠缠纠错机制," which automatically adjusts entangled parameters based on real-time quantum state fluctuations. This adaptive control offers a significant improvement over static approaches, potentially unlocking new possibilities in secure communication and complex computation. The study explores the design and validation of this protocol, focusing on its ability to maintain entanglement fidelity and achieve enhanced communication rates.

title: Contextual Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Memory Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to reinforcement learning, termed Contextual Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Memory Networks (CRLHMN), designed to overcome the challenges inherent in long-horizon tasks and limited memory capacity within traditional reinforcement learning paradigms. The core idea is to integrate contextual reinforcement learning (CRL) with a hierarchical memory network architecture. This allows the agent to not only learn from immediate rewards but also to maintain and retrieve contextual information, significantly enhancing decision-making in complex, dynamic environments. The proposed system leverages hierarchical memory to represent and access knowledge at multiple levels of abstraction, facilitating efficient learning and adaptation. The system is evaluated theoretically and conceptually, outlining its potential benefits and future research directions. The primary contribution lies in the synergistic combination of these two approaches, promising improved performance in scenarios requiring both long-term planning and contextual understanding.

title: ##混沌几何的自适应优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization algorithm based on the principles of chaos theory, specifically focusing on adaptive optimization. We introduce a framework wherein the optimization problem is dynamically transformed into a chaotic system, allowing the algorithm to adapt to local perturbations and achieve high efficiency. The core mechanism involves iteratively refining the chaotic system through a self-organizing optimization process, effectively mitigating the influence of noise and ensuring convergence to optimal solutions. This approach distinguishes itself from conventional methods by leveraging the inherent dynamics of chaos to provide a robust and adaptable solution strategy. The theoretical underpinnings of the algorithm, including the concept of Lyapunov stability and chaos theory's role in efficient optimization, are discussed. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through illustrative examples and preliminary analysis, establishing its potential for significant improvements in various optimization scenarios.

title: The Number That Finds Your Match: A Narrative Review of Skill Rating and Matchmaking from Elo's Chess to TrueSkill 2
abstract: Skill rating and matchmaking---the mathematics that turns thousands of scattered players into fair pairings---moved from Elo's 1978 chess rating through Glickman's dynamic estimation, Herbrich and colleagues's Bayesian TrueSkill, and Coulom's whole-history rating to the game industry's architectures, the evolutionary optimization of fairness, and TrueSkill 2's team models. This article presents a narrative review of that arc's canonical line: Elo's 1978 The Rating of Chessplayers, Batchelder and Bershad's 1979 statistical theory, Glickman's 1999 dynamic estimation, Glickman and Jones's 1999 evaluation, Herbrich, Minka, and Graepel's 2006 TrueSkill, Feng, Brandt, and Saha's 2007 matchmaking architecture, Dangauthier and colleagues's 2008 TrueSkill through time, Coulom's 2008 whole-history rating, Menke and Martinez's 2008 MCMC model, Chen and colleagues's 2017 evolutionary matchmaking, Minka, Cleven, and Zaykov's 2018 TrueSkill 2, and Kovalchik's 2020 margin-of-victory extension. The review is organized around three themes: the chess foundations, in which the rating table's logistic update, the paired-comparison statistics, and the system's evaluation made the skill a number; the Bayesian era, in which the multiplayer extensions, the histories' re-estimation, and the posterior's sampling made the uncertainty a first-class citizen; and the game industry's systems, in which the architectures' scaling, the evolutionary fairness's optimization, and the margins' and teams' models carried the mathematics into the lobbies. It is concluded that skill rating is the fairness's information system---and that its arc is the number's evolution from the scalar's chess to the Bayesian's teams.

title: Chatbots in Educational Settings
abstract: Chatbots, also called conversational agents, have rapidly evolved from simple rule-based systems into advanced AI-driven tools that can support teaching and learning through natural language interaction and adaptive guidance. Their use in education has grown quickly, yet current research remains fragmented, narrow in scope, and often limited in design. This makes it difficult to form a clear understanding of their educational potential and to identify common patterns across studies. The goal of this scoping review is to address this gap by bringing together recent research on how chatbots have been used in education, focusing on their roles, design strategies, interaction methods, and ultimately contributions to learner engagement. The review shows that most studies are applied in language and STEM field at the secondary and undergraduate levels, often targeting adolescents and young adults. Many rely on cross-sectional or quasi-experimental designs, self-report data, and only limited use of theoretical frameworks. While findings suggest that chatbots can enhance behavioral, cognitive, and emotional engagement, important challenges, such as emotional scaffolding, cognitive load, and diverse learner needs, remain underexplored. By synthesizing this body of work, the review provides educators, developers, and policymakers with a clearer understanding of the current landscape and practical guidance for designing future research and implementations.

title: brnltk: a python toolkit for processing bangla regional dialects
abstract: Bangla is a morphologically rich, low-resource language whose regional dialects suffer from an even greater scarcity of tools, corpora, and annotated datasets. This paper introduces brnltk, the first modular Python toolkit designed for processing Bangla regional dialects. It integrates rule-based, statistical, and neural components for dialect translation, POS tagging, stemming, tokenization, and semantic similarity computation across five regions: Mymensingh, Barishal, Chattogram, Noakhali, and Sylhet. POS tagging reaches up to 96% accuracy, exceeding a general-purpose Bangla baseline (50.8%); dialect translation attains chrF 25.0–54.1, BLEU 1.4–13.4, METEOR 11.2–37.5, WER up to 89.4%, and CER up to 64.3% across dialect pairs. Training-free for end users and built on human-verified dialectal mappings, brnltk requires no annotated corpora or fine-tuning.

title: Authority Bias in Conversational Search Engines for Academic Paper Recommendation
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as conversational search engines for academic literature, yet whether they judge papers on content or on authority signals has not been tested causally. We investigate authority bias: systematic preference for papers based on author prestige, venue, and citations rather than content. Holding title and abstract constant, we vary authority metadata across three counterfactual conditions (original, flipped, boosted) over eight LLMs (five open-weight and three frontier closed-weight) in an in-context, single-turn, top-1 recommendation setting. Our experiments show that authority bias is substantial and directional, varies markedly across models, and is only partially addressable through prompt-level debiasing. We further document a say-do gap: debiasing instructions suppress authority mentions far faster than authority-driven flips, so surface auditing systematically underestimates behavioral bias.

title: Generative multi-domain transfer learning for fault detection in data-scarce wind turbines
abstract: Normal behavior models have shown promise for reliable fault detection in wind turbines. However, these unsupervised anomaly detection models require sufficient fault-free training data to learn the normal operation behavior of turbines. Under data scarcity, for example in newly deployed wind turbines, these models may result in poor fault detection performance. In this work, we propose a multi-domain generative domain mapping approach based on Star Generative Adversarial Networks (StarGAN) to improve fault detection on data-scarce wind turbines. Our model maps SCADA measurements from a data-scarce turbine to resemble those of several data-rich turbines. By preserving the operational state during translation, faults occurring in a data-scarce domain can be mapped and detected by reliable pre-trained normal behavior models of data-rich domains. Highlighting the benefits of an ensemble fusion strategy, we show that under severe data scarcity our method can produce anomaly scores comparable to models trained on large representative datasets. Our approach can consistently outperform models trained on scarce data when less than 2 weeks of training data are available. With just 2 weeks of accumulated training data, we achieve an anomaly score similarity that is, on average, +16% higher than conventional fine-tuning, and +10% higher than single-source domain mapping. As a step towards unsupervised model selection, we propose a proxy metric that detects poor performance at training time, despite an absence of anomalies. Our study presents the potential and challenges of multi-domain mapping for wind turbine fault detection under unrepresentative training data.

title: NEURO-ALGORITHMIC CONSUMER INSIGHTS: INTEGRATING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, NEUROMARKETING, AND PERSONALIZED MARKETING - A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK AND SIMULATION-BASED PROOF OF CONCEPT
abstract: There is an increasing tendency in marketing practices of using artificial intelligence (AI) for message personalization while neuromarketing can provide data on consumer behavior that are impossible to obtain from self-reports. Despite similarities, the fields have been developing separately. This paper presents the Neuro-Algorithmic Consumer Insights (NACI) model where AI-based personalization leads to physiological responses (arousal, motivation for an approach, attention), which influence the results from self-reports of emotional response to purchase execution. The results can be further used as predictors of purchase behavior. For the verification of the proposed model, an experiment was conducted with 600 subjects (289 personalized messages and 311 generic). The analysis included Welch tests with Holm correction, hierarchical regression, bootstrapped mediation analysis, and multiple logistic regression. It was demonstrated that personalization leads to arousal (d = 0.45), greater left frontal alpha asymmetry (d = 0.431), attention (d = 0.24), engagement (d = 0.40), and intention to purchase (d = 0.37). It was found that physiological variables can account for 24.1% of variability in intention to purchase over demographic and personalization variables (F(4, 590) = 52.11, p < .001). It is estimated that attention and engagement accounted for 59 percent of the overall effect. Incorporation of physiological factors resulted in the increase in cross-validated AUC for purchase from .61 to .69 according to logistic regression. The results indicate that the designed pipeline reveals previously confirmed effects but does not yield novel insights. The article also reviews limitations of the research and deals with ethical issues raised by it.

title: Quantum Topology Geometry Parameter Optimization
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field of mathematics, offers a novel approach to designing quantum systems with enhanced properties. This paper investigates a novel optimization algorithm, Quantum Topology Geometry Parameter Optimization (QTGPO), based on the principles of quantum topology. The algorithm leverages the inherent geometric properties of quantum states to guide parameter adjustments, ultimately aiming to improve quantum computation accuracy and efficiency. We propose a mechanism for systematically optimizing key parameters within a quantum system, guided by the underlying topology of the system. The core claim centers on the development of this algorithm as a means to overcome limitations in traditional optimization methods, particularly in the context of quantum systems. This paper explores the theoretical underpinnings of QTGPO and presents preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in a specific quantum system.

title: 基于贝叶斯网络的不确定性推理与决策
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Bayesian networks for uncertainty reasoning and decision-making. In complex systems characterized by incomplete and uncertain information, traditional deterministic methods often prove inadequate. Bayesian networks, leveraging probabilistic inference, provide a powerful framework for representing and reasoning with such uncertainties. This work outlines a methodology for constructing Bayesian networks to model key factors influencing a system, followed by the application of Bayesian inference algorithms to derive probabilities and ultimately, inform decisions. The core contribution lies in utilizing the inherent probabilistic reasoning capabilities of Bayesian networks to enhance decision reliability compared to alternative approaches like fuzzy logic or expert systems. Specifically, we explore how to translate real-world scenarios into a network structure, quantify relationships with conditional probabilities, and then employ inference algorithms to update beliefs and arrive at optimal or well-supported decisions. The focus is on the theoretical aspects and the overall framework, without empirical validation through experimentation.

title: Non-Local Topology for Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of non-local topology to enhance the representational capabilities of neural networks. Traditional neural networks often struggle with complex patterns and nuanced relationships, limiting their ability to learn intricate data representations. We propose a novel topology – the "Dynamic Flow Network" (DFN) – designed to facilitate this propagation of information across network nodes, enabling the model to capture more complex dependencies and improve overall performance. We explore the benefits of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments demonstrating improved generalization and robustness. The core claim is that the DFN significantly boosts representational capacity, leading to better learning outcomes.

title: Dynamic Probability Field: A Graph-Based Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic probability field optimization algorithm designed to enhance machine learning model performance, particularly in scenarios with sparse data. Traditional approaches often rely on manual parameter adjustment, limiting automation. The core of this algorithm lies in framing the probability field as a graph, leveraging its inherent structure and parameter adjustments to dynamically optimize model performance. We propose a mechanism that iteratively adjusts probability field parameters based on feedback from the training data, promoting better generalization. The algorithm's novelty stems from its automated adaptation of probability field parameters, circumventing the limitations of manual tuning.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning for Dynamic Knowledge Graph Construction
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for constructing dynamic knowledge graphs (KGs) through neuro-symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to build a system capable of automatically learning and reasoning from data, concurrently updating the KG structure. This is achieved by integrating neural networks for symbolic reasoning and leveraging KGs for data-driven learning. Existing neuro-symbolic approaches often rely on pre-defined, manually curated KGs, limiting their adaptability and scalability. Our system addresses this limitation by enabling automated KG construction and dynamic evolution. We present a methodology that utilizes neural networks to represent and manipulate symbolic rules, while the KG serves as a repository for learned facts and relationships. The system learns by iteratively refining its symbolic rules based on observed data and KG consistency, resulting in a robust and evolving knowledge representation. This framework offers significant advantages over traditional KG construction methods and provides a foundation for intelligent systems capable of adapting to changing information landscapes. The key contributions of this work include a novel architecture combining neural and symbolic reasoning, a dynamic KG update mechanism, and a methodology for learning from data to enhance the KG's accuracy and completeness.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Non-linear Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-linear optimization algorithm based on quantum entanglement principles. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, non-linear problems, demanding extensive manual tuning. This algorithm leverages quantum entanglement to establish a dynamic interaction between parameters, enabling a more adaptive and robust solution strategy. We propose a mechanism that iteratively adjusts parameters based on entanglement correlations, facilitating the exploration of complex solution spaces and improving the performance of various optimization tasks, particularly those encountered in machine learning, financial modeling, and risk management. The core of this approach lies in the manipulation of entanglement to achieve a more efficient and nuanced optimization process. This research explores the potential of quantum entanglement to surpass the limitations of classical optimization techniques.

abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has emerged as a transformative paradigm, offering the potential to revolutionize data analysis and machine learning. This paper explores a novel quantum machine learning framework, "Dynamic Quantum State," designed to address challenges associated with data distribution, noise, and non-linearity. We propose a mechanism leveraging quantum state manipulation to dynamically generate and optimize the search space, leading to smoother data distributions and enhanced resilience to perturbations. The core claim is that this framework enables efficient data handling and effective solution exploration, surpassing the limitations of conventional machine learning approaches.

title: 基于自适应自旋的量子计算的非线性拓扑扩展
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive spin qubit technology to enhance the efficiency of quantum computation. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on meticulous design and calibration, limiting their scalability and versatility. We propose a novel approach leveraging dynamically adjusted spin qubit configurations through adaptive self-sensing and manipulation. This system aims to overcome limitations of current quantum algorithms by enabling efficient exploration of complex, non-linear topological structures. The core mechanism involves a sophisticated feedback loop that adjusts the qubit's spin state based on real-time data, promoting the formation of intricate and robust topological states. This approach has the potential to significantly increase the computational depth and complexity of quantum computations, offering a pathway towards more powerful and reliable quantum systems. We present a preliminary simulation demonstrating the efficacy of this method.

title: Title: Geometric Chaos Optimization with Adaptive Parameter Tuning
abstract: Geometric chaos, a phenomenon observed in various physical systems, introduces inherent unpredictability in the search space for optimal solutions. This paper explores a novel optimization algorithm, Geometric Chaos Optimization with Adaptive Parameter Tuning, designed to exploit this behavior by employing a probabilistic parameter adjustment mechanism. We posit that by dynamically adjusting parameters based on the observed chaotic tendencies of the solution, we can navigate complex search spaces more effectively than traditional optimization methods. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of deterministic algorithms by introducing a degree of flexibility and adaptability, particularly in scenarios with high dimensionality and intricate dependencies. The core mechanism hinges on a probabilistic model that quantifies the 'chaotic' behavior, allowing for a targeted refinement of the search process. This paper presents a detailed theoretical analysis and a practical implementation of this algorithm, demonstrating its effectiveness in a series of benchmark problems, highlighting the potential for improved performance in complex optimization challenges.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Memory Coding (QEMC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to memory storage and retrieval, termed Quantum Entanglement-Based Memory Coding (QEMC). The core claim is that quantum entanglement offers a pathway to encoding complex memory information with unprecedented density and redundancy, surpassing the limitations of conventional classical methods. The proposed mechanism leverages different entanglement bases for distinct memory elements and manipulates entanglement states to represent memory states. The inherent properties of quantum entanglement – the ability to store multiple pieces of information simultaneously and extract the entire entangled state through measurement of a single quantum bit – are central to this approach. QEMC represents a fundamentally new paradigm in information storage, potentially unlocking capabilities for vastly denser and more resilient memory systems. This work outlines the theoretical framework and key concepts behind QEMC, highlighting its potential impact on future memory technologies.

title: Dynamic Topological Adaptive Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum computing termed "Dynamic Topological Adaptive Quantum Computing," addressing the limitations of static quantum architectures. The core concept revolves around the ability of a quantum topology to dynamically reshape itself based on input data, maximizing efficiency in quantum algorithm execution. This is achieved by leveraging entangled states within a quantum topological network, coupled with machine learning algorithms. These algorithms enable real-time adjustments to quantum bit connectivity and gate operations, optimizing both circuit pathways and overall efficiency. Unlike existing quantum computing paradigms reliant on fixed topologies, this adaptive system represents a significant advancement, offering the potential for dramatically improved performance and scalability. The theoretical framework presented outlines the key components and operational principles, highlighting the potential for a fundamentally new approach to quantum computation. We explore the mathematical underpinnings of this system, focusing on the control and manipulation of entangled states and the optimization of quantum circuits.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Betsileo Woolly Lemur Algorithm" (BWLA), inspired by the foraging and social behavior of *Hapalemur betsileuzi*, the Betsileo woolly lemur. These lemurs exhibit unique strategies for resource acquisition and group dynamics, particularly regarding territorial defense and opportunistic feeding. BWLA leverages these behavioral traits to develop a robust and efficient optimization method. The algorithm incorporates elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA) combined with a novel "territorial defense" mechanism and a "social influence" component. We present the algorithm's theoretical foundation, its implementation, and demonstrate its effectiveness on a range of benchmark optimization problems. The results indicate that BWLA consistently performs competitively with established metaheuristic algorithms, demonstrating its potential as a valuable tool for solving complex optimization challenges. The key contributions of this work include a new approach to metaheuristic design grounded in animal behavioral analysis and a thorough evaluation of the algorithm's performance across diverse problem landscapes.

title: Bawean Deer Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Bawean Deer Behavior
abstract: This paper presents the Bawean Deer Algorithm (BDA), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Bawean deer, a unique deer species endemic to Indonesia. BDA leverages the deer's strategic movement patterns, including rotational searching, memory retention, and adaptation to environmental changes, to develop a robust optimization strategy. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a 'deer herd' to explore the search space. Each deer's movement is governed by a combination of random exploration and exploitation, guided by a 'memory' mechanism that stores the best-found solutions. The algorithm's parameters, including step size, memory size, and rotation frequency, are dynamically adjusted based on the fitness landscape. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BDA through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The key features of BDA are its adaptive movement strategy, memory-based learning, and dynamic parameter tuning, which contribute to its ability to effectively navigate complex and multimodal optimization landscapes. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. Future research directions include exploring the algorithm's applicability to different problem domains and further refining its parameter tuning mechanism.

title: Bartels's Rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Animal's Navigation Strategy
abstract: This paper introduces Bartels's Rat, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the navigational strategy of Bartels's rat, a European rodent known for its remarkable ability to find its way back to a known location after being displaced. The algorithm leverages the rat's reliance on scent trails and probabilistic movement to efficiently explore the solution space. Bartels's Rat utilizes a particle representation, analogous to the rat's scent trail, and employs a probabilistic movement strategy based on the inverse square root of the distance to the target. The algorithm incorporates a learning mechanism, mimicking the rat's adaptation to scent concentration, to guide exploration and exploitation. We present a detailed description of the algorithm, its underlying principles, and its performance on a variety of benchmark optimization problems. Experimental results demonstrate that Bartels's Rat exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods, particularly in problems with high dimensionality and complex landscapes. The algorithm's simplicity and adaptability make it a promising candidate for a wide range of optimization challenges.

title: Quantum Networking: Information Encoding and Decoding Strategies
abstract: This paper investigates optimal information encoding and decoding strategies within quantum networks. The core aim is to enhance information transmission efficiency and security by leveraging principles from information theory and quantum information theory. We analyze various encoding and decoding schemes, quantifying their performance using key metrics such as channel capacity and quantum bit error rate (QBER). This work focuses on identifying strategies that maximize the fidelity of quantum information transfer, considering the inherent challenges posed by quantum noise and decoherence. The proposed strategies incorporate adaptive coding techniques and error correction protocols tailored to specific network topologies and noise characteristics. Ultimately, this research contributes to the development of more robust and efficient quantum networks, a critical component of future quantum communication systems.

title: Non-Classical Computation for Cognitive Map Construction
abstract: This paper explores the potential of non-classical computation, specifically quantum computing, to construct cognitive maps and simulate human cognitive processes. Traditional cognitive models often struggle to accurately represent the complexity and interconnectedness of human knowledge. We propose a novel approach utilizing quantum graphs, leveraging quantum entanglement to represent and model cognitive elements and their relationships. These graphs, denoted as (s1, s2, ..., sK), provide a framework for capturing the nuanced interactions within a cognitive system. The core mechanism relies on the entanglement between nodes, where the degree of entanglement directly reflects the strength of the associated cognitive connection. This approach offers a fundamentally different perspective on cognition, potentially overcoming limitations inherent in classical computational models. The paper details the theoretical framework, explores key concepts, and outlines the potential benefits and future directions of this research. ---

BMB-MOA incorporates three key mechanisms: Color Shift Adaptation (CSA), Directional Flight Adjustment (DFA), and Adaptive Velocity Control (AVC). CSA dynamically adjusts the exploration and exploitation balance, DFA guides the search towards promising regions of the solution space, and AVC controls the velocity of the search agents, promoting efficient convergence. title: Adaptive Machine Learning via Biofeedback Signals
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of integrating biofeedback signals into machine learning algorithms to achieve adaptive learning. The core concept involves leveraging physiological data, such as heart rate variability (HRV) and electroencephalography (EEG), to dynamically adjust the learning process. We explore two primary mechanisms: utilizing biofeedback as a reward signal within reinforcement learning frameworks and incorporating it as a regularization term in standard machine learning algorithms. The aim is to enhance the performance and robustness of these algorithms by allowing them to respond to the learner's internal state and cognitive load. The proposed approach offers a novel pathway to create more intelligent and adaptable systems, particularly in scenarios where the learning environment is complex or the learner's needs are constantly changing. The theoretical framework and potential applications are discussed, highlighting the key challenges and future research directions.
