title: Beyond Bio-Inspired Algorithms: Using Bird Landing Dynamics to Design Adaptive Parameter Control in Metaheuristics
abstract: Bio-inspiration has mainly been used to represent organisms, behaviors, or natural processes in the design of metaheuristics. This study proposes a different use: drawing on a biological phenomenon to model the temporal evolution of an internal parameter in an existing algorithm. Logarithmic Mean Optimization (LMO) is adopted as a case study, focusing on β, which scales the stochastic perturbation term and regulates the balance between exploration and exploitation. Inspired by the progressive transition observed during bird landing, a normalized arctangent trajectory controlled by m and k is proposed. Both hyperparameters were tuned through Bayesian optimization using the Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) implemented in Optuna. The 23 benchmark functions were divided into 12 tuning functions and 11 independent test functions. Nine β configurations were evaluated through 31 runs per function. The Friedman test showed significant differences among the variants (p=3.8269×10−10), and the proposed formulation achieved the best average rank (1.7273). Post-hoc Wilcoxon tests with Holm correction found significant differences against two of the eight alternatives. Overall, the results suggest that bio-inspiration, when used as a criterion for designing adaptive parameter-control mechanisms, can yield improvements and be considered a potential alternative in the design of new metaheuristic algorithms.

title: A Comparative Experiment on Authorship Attribution Between AI andHumans and Its Humanistic Implications
abstract: 이 연구는 대규모 언어모델(LLM)의 등장이 저자 판별 연구에 가져온 방법론적 전환을 실험적으로 검토한다. 이를 위해 조건이 상반되는 두 편의 근대 한국어 텍스트, 즉 후보 저자군과 참조 텍스트가 충분히 확보된 「조선민시론」(1922)과 후보 저자군을 특정할 수 없고 참조 텍스트를 확보하는 것도 매우 어려운 「참말로 잇든 처녀들의 동맹휴학」(1926)을 대상으로, 계량적 언어자질 기반의 인간 연구자 저자 판별 결과와 LLM(ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini)이 수행한 저자 판별 결과를 비교하였다. 「조선민시론」의 경우 ChatGPT는 후보 저자군을 압축해서 제시하지 않았음에도 80-90%의 확률로 최남선을 저자로 지목하였으며, 이는 후보군을 최남선·염상섭 2인으로 압축하여 97%의 확률을 보고한 기존 계량적 연구(김일환 외 2025)와 방향성에서 일치하는 결과였다. 반면 후보 저자군과 참조 덱스트가 모두 부재한 「참말로 잇든 처녀들의 동맹휴학」의 경우, LLM은 확정적인 저자를 제시하는 대신 장르 판정과 서사 시점 분석, 어휘·문체 지표를 결합한 저자 프로파일링을 통해 저자의 속성(성별, 직업, 이념적 성향)을 추정하는 데 그쳤다. 이는 참조 텍스트가 뒷받침되지 않는 상황에서 LLM에 성급한 확정적 판별을 요구할 경우 역사적 사실에 부합하지 않는 환각(hallucination)이 발생할 위험이 있음을 시사한다. 이러한 결과를 토대로 본 연구는 LLM 기반 저자 판별이 인간 연구자를 대체하는 도구가 아니라 가설 생성과 정성적 해석을 보완하는 협업적 도구로 자리매김해야 함을 제안하며, AGI로의 기술적 전환 속에서 인문학에 요구되는 human-in-the-loop 방법론에 대해 논의한다.

title: Reinforcement learning optimization of a 6 Li magneto-optical trap: DDPG versus SAC
abstract: We report an experimental implementation of deep reinforcement learning (RL) for optimizing the loading stage of a 6 Li magneto-optical trap (MOT) in a high-dimensional continuous control space. An off-policy actor-critic agent observes in-situ fluorescence images at 111 ms intervals and updates seven experimental parameters over 18 decision steps. Learning is performed directly on the apparatus using a sparse terminal reward R = N × A extracted from an absorption image, where N is the atom number, and A is the peak optical depth. We benchmark Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) across three independent 300-episode training runs under identical alignment. Both algorithms surpass the human-optimized (HO) baseline, but the central finding concerns reliability rather than peak performance. In deterministic replay validation, the three SAC waveforms show reward coefficients of variation of 9–14%, and the minimum reward of each waveform exceeds the HO mean reward. The DDPG waveforms show up to three times the dispersion, and even the best-performing DDPG run contains a catastrophic near-zero shot. The SAC solutions are nearly time-independent and consistently converge to a blue-detuned repump laser with an elevated field gradient, reminiscent of compressed-MOT operating conditions. Our results show that off-policy actor-critic RL can autonomously optimize high-dimensional laser-cooling sequences in an operating ultracold-atom apparatus, and that SAC has a reproducibility advantage over DDPG in a real noisy environment.

title: Language-Informed Flow Matching for Trend-Guided Structure-Based 3D Molecular Generation
abstract: Structure-based drug design (SBDD) requires ligands that satisfy both 3D target affinity and 1D chemical validity. Existing controllable generation methods often rely on task-specific fine-tuning or externally imposed sampling-time guidance, adding cost and potentially conflicting with evolving 3D geometric constraints. We propose LiFT, a language-informed cross-modal framework built on Flow Matching for trend-guided 3D molecular generation across both de novo design and scaffold hopping. LiFT uses a "Sense-Evolve-Assemble" agent to generate target-aware SMILES as intermediate chemical conditions, from which a pre-trained chemical foundation model extracts continuous semantic priors. These priors are integrated into geometric generation through a lightweight semantic projector with zero-initialized adaptive normalization for stable cross-modal conditioning. We further introduce a Self-Conditioned Decoupled Router (SCDR), which modulates the velocity field according to intermediate structural states during ODE integration. Experiments on Cross-Docked2020 show that LiFT achieves competitive distribution matching while improving medicinal chemistry metrics and maintaining competitive structural validity under task-steering settings without additional generator fine-tuning. Our results suggest that language-derived chemical priors provide effective trend-level guidance for 3D molecular generation. Code and released artifacts are available at https://github.com/kasurl/LiFT.

evidence.title: Language-Informed Flow Matching for Trend-Guided Structure-Based 3D Molecular Generation
evidence.abstract: Structure-based drug design (SBDD) requires ligands that satisfy both 3D target affinity and 1D chemical validity. Existing controllable generation methods often rely on task-specific fine-tuning or externally imposed sampling-time guidance, adding cost and potentially conflicting with evolving 3D geometric constraints. We propose LiFT, a language-informed cross-modal framework built on Flow Matching for trend-guided 3D molecular generation across both de novo design and scaffold hopping. LiFT uses a "Sense-Evolve-Assemble" agent to generate target-aware SMILES as intermediate chemical conditions, from which a pre-trained chemical foundation model extracts continuous semantic priors. These priors are integrated into geometric generation through a lightweight semantic projector with zero-initialized adaptive normalization for stable cross-modal conditioning. We further introduce a Self-Conditioned Decoupled Router (SCDR), which modulates the velocity field according to intermediate structural states during ODE integration. Experiments on Cross-Docked2020 show that LiFT achieves competitive distribution matching while improving medicinal chemistry metrics and maintaining competitive structural validity under task-steering settings without additional generator fine-tuning. Our results suggest that language-derived chemical priors provide effective trend-level guidance for 3D molecular generation. Code and released artifacts are available at https://github.com/kasurl/LiFT.

title: Learning from What You Retrieve: Online RL Fine-Tuning for Semantic Retrieval
abstract: In large-scale e-commerce retrieval, dual-encoder retrievers are op- timized for contrastive similarity, whereas downstream rerankers capture finer-grained relevance preferences; this objective mis- match limits end-to-end retrieval quality. Reinforcement Learning offers a way to use reward-model feedback for retriever adaptation, but we observe that standard policy-gradient updates can degrade embedding geometry, especially when the document index must remain frozen due to industrial constraints. To address this, we propose PAO (Positive-Advantage-Only), a selective RL optimization method. Our analysis reveals that in- discriminate penalization of negative samples (pushing away) in a frozen high-dimensional space disrupts pre-trained semantic man- ifolds. PAO selectively applies gradient updates only to retrieved items with positive advantages, effectively pulling query embed- dings toward high-reward regions while preserving global topo- logical stability. Experiments on both a massive industrial dataset and public benchmarks demonstrate that PAO significantly outper- forms standard RL and distillation baselines.

title: Learning-Assisted Congestion-Aware Route Scheduling for Semiconductor Fab Material Control Systems
abstract: Automated material handling systems in semiconductor fabs are operated by a material control system (MCS) that must schedule a relay route for every transport command online, before execution. This is a data-driven scheduling problem in which route cost is dominated in the upper tail by queueing at heterogeneous, partially observable relay equipment, so route selection requires estimating both delivery time and congestion risk at the decision moment. This paper proposes a transport-network-aware dynamic congestion representation (TN-DCR). Built on a static directed transport graph induced by historically observed relay segments, TN-DCR combines structural route priors, multi-window network-wide congestion context, route-level bottleneck exposure, and an inductive graph-aware route embedding, all constructed under a prediction-time-safety invariant that admits only information observed strictly before the prediction moment. The representation feeds separate queue- and transfer-time regressors and an ordinal multi-label classifier producing calibrated multi-threshold exceedance scores, with an empirical-Bayes stock-key residual correction reducing systematic queue-time underprediction. The predictions serve as costs in a risk-constrained route-scheduling rule that minimizes predicted delivery time subject to a bound on extreme-congestion probability, embedding the learned predictors within a lightweight operations-research decision model. In a controlled closed-loop evaluation, mean delivery time falls by 16.4\% and internal resource waiting time by 22.6\% while throughput remains essentially unchanged.

title: Online Estimation of Dynamic Origin-Destination Matrices Using Reinforcement Learning with Link-Flow Propagation Guidance
abstract: Dynamic origin-destination (OD) matrix estimation calibrates time-dependent input demand for simulations to reproduce observed link flows. Reinforcement learning is well suited to online estimation because a trained policy estimates demand in a single evaluation, but varying target flows complicate learning from aggregate rewards. We propose reinforcement learning with link-flow propagation guidance (LFPG-RL), combining simulated vehicle propagation records with downstream errors to guide individual OD components. Using 250 weekday link-flow trajectories from a Melbourne arterial network, LFPG-RL achieves a mean test root mean squared error (RMSE) of 7.41 vehicles per 15-minute interval, mean absolute percentage error of 31.24%, and Pearson correlation of 0.987. Comparisons with optimisation, filtering and reinforcement learning without guidance show a 40.1% RMSE reduction over the strongest baseline, gradient descent with propagation guidance. LFPG-RL enables rapid demand updates that keep traffic simulations consistent with observed conditions, supporting the evaluation of traffic management strategies.

title: Data Risk Factor Classification of Aviation Accident Reports Based on Multilingual Topic Modeling
abstract: 본 연구는 미국과 한국의 항공사고 및 준사고 보고서를 통합 분석하여 사고 유형별 핵심 위험 요인을 정량적으로 도출하는 것을 목적으로 한다. 이를 위해 NTSB, ASRS 및 한국 항공·철도사고조사위원회의 보고서 총3,471건을 수집하고, 다국어 문장 임베딩-BERTopic 기반 토픽 모델링-제로샷 분류 및 규칙 기반 보정으로 이어지는 통합 텍스트 마이닝 프레임워크를 구축하여 분석을 수행하였다. 분석 결과, 총 112개의 토픽이 추출되었으며 활주로 이탈, 비행 중 제어 상실, 추진계통 결함, 난기류, 지상 충돌이 주요 사고 유형으로 식별되었다. 추가적으로 제로샷 분류와 도메인 규칙을 활용해 국제 표준 분류체계에 매핑한 결과, Top-1 기준 81.5%의 높은 분류 정확도를 달성하였다. 또한 국가별 비교를 통해 미국 보고서는 조종사 관점의 절차적 오류 및 인적 요인이, 한국 보고서는 기상 및 기체 등 기술적 요인이 주로 강조되는 차이를 확인하였다. 본 연구는 다국어 텍스트 마이닝 프레임워크를 구축하여 언어적 차이를 극복하고 텍스트 기반 사고 분석을 자동화할 수 있는 가능성을 실증했다는 점에서 의의가 있다.

title: D3.2 Public report on AI adoption
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming research, industry, and public services across Europe. Advances in foundation models, generative AI, and emerging agentic AI systems have accelerated interest in AI adoption, while simultaneously exposing organisations to new challenges related to computing infrastructure, data governance, skills development, regulatory compliance, sustainability, and operational deployment. As Europe seeks to strengthen its technological sovereignty and trustworthy AI capabilities through initiatives such as the AI Act, EuroHPC, AI Factories, and AI Gigafactories, there is a growing need to understand the practical realities of AI adoption. This deliverable presents the experiences and observations collected by the technical AI experts (WP3) of the LUMI AI Factory (LUMI AIF) during its first 18 months of operation. Drawing on customer consultations, support activities, customer surveys, and selected use cases, the report analyses how organisations move from interest in AI towards experimentation, scaling, and operational deployment. The findings show that AI adoption is advancing across a wide range of sectors. While generative AI and large language models currently attract the greatest attention, many organisations continue to rely on traditional machine learning methods, predictive analytics, and data analysis. Also, the integration of advanced computational simulation and AI methods, a horizontal focus area of LUMI AIF, is gaining increased attention. The report highlights the important role of advanced computing infrastructures such as LUMI in supporting AI adoption. High-performance computing enables large-scale model training, batch inference, simulation–AI integration, and extensive experimentation that would be difficult or prohibitively expensive elsewhere. Still, successful AI adoption depends on more than hardware. Expert consultation, customer training, data services, software environments, and ecosystem collaboration are equally important components. Indeed, customer interactions reveal that the most significant barriers to adoption are often not the AI models themselves or access to suitable computing resources. Recurring challenges include data availability and quality, management of sensitive and confidential information, regulatory uncertainty, limited skills, and difficulties in transitioning successful prototypes into production systems. Many customers require guidance in formulating AI-ready problems, selecting appropriate infrastructure, understanding regulatory obligations, and developing sustainable deployment strategies. Looking ahead, the report identifies six priority areas for future AI adoption support: stronger assistance with early-stage problem formulation, improved support for data readiness and governance, more accessible pathways to advanced computing infrastructure, better guidance for the transition from experimentation to production, focus on practical AI literacy and comprehensive skills development, and continued coordination with the other European initiatives. Overall, the report concludes that successful AI adoption requires an integrated ecosystem approach. Access to computing resources alone is insufficient. Organisations need a combination of infrastructure, expertise, data services, skills development, trusted governance mechanisms, and ecosystem support to translate AI opportunities into sustainable and impactful outcomes. Through its infrastructure, consultation services, customer training activities, and collaboration with the wider European AI ecosystem, LUMI AIF is contributing to Europe's future AI capabilities. This document is under review.

title: tanager-minmap: mineral and mine-waste mapping from Planet Tanager VSWIR surface reflectance
abstract: Analysis code and derivative mineral-mapping products from tanager-minmap, a reproducible workflow that maps alteration and mine-waste minerals from Planet Tanager 426-band visible-to-shortwave-infrared (VSWIR) surface reflectance at two US mining districts: Goldfield, Nevada, and Bingham Canyon, Utah. tanager-minmap-v0.1.1.zip — complete source at release v0.1.1: the seven-stage pipeline and command-line tool, test suite, technical memo, slide deck, story page, figures, and interactive maps. tanager-minmap-derivative-maps-v0.1.1.zip — 44 GeoTIFF derivative rasters (continuum-removed band-depth maps, MTMF abundance and infeasibility maps per target mineral, and the Bingham surface-mineralogical screening tiers) plus the headline result tables and an attribution README. Code is MIT licensed. The derivative rasters are adapted Planet material distributed under CC BY 4.0 with the required notices: "Adapted from Tanager STAC Data, available at www.planet.com/data/stac © 2024 Planet Labs PBC. All Rights Reserved." and "Adapted from Tanager STAC Data, available at www.planet.com/data/stac © 2025 Planet Labs PBC. All Rights Reserved." The EMIT comparison derives from NASA EMIT L2A reflectance (doi:10.5067/EMIT/EMITL2ARFL.001); the alteration-map comparison uses Rockwell & Bonham (2017, doi:10.5066/F7CR5RK7); mineral references are from the USGS Spectral Library v7 (splib07a; Kokaly et al. 2017, doi:10.3133/ds1035). Story page: fossettlab.github.io/tanager-minmap · Repository: github.com/fossettlab/tanager-minmap Version 0.1.1 is the harmonized submission-day snapshot: identical rasters and results to v0.1.0, with the final wording of the memo, story page, and deck as submitted via the project website on 2026-08-31.

title: k-jinma/dogo-tutor: dogo-tutor v0.0.2 - Initial Release
abstract: This is the initial release of "dogo-tutor," an AI tutor designed for coding education. This release is created to archive the repository and obtain a DOI via Zenodo. Key Features Provides step-by-step hints (problem clarification, strategy, logic structuring, and partial code) rather than direct answers. Designed to offer deeper hints only when students explain "what they tried and what happened" in their own words. Automatically generates review notes and short quizzes (/review) based on the last 24 hours of dialogue history, focusing on concepts the student struggled with. Features a self-reflection tool (/log) that allows students to objectively track their dependency on deep hints. Employs a safe guidance design that strictly references URLs from actual lecture materials and official documentation specified by the instructor. Recent Changes Revamped the README for users and added an English summary. Adjusted the icon design for the VS Code extension. Updated various configuration files (e.g., package.json) for public release.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding: An Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two particles become linked regardless of distance, presents a potentially revolutionary approach to information security. This paper explores the utilization of quantum entanglement to develop an adaptive algorithm for key distribution, aiming to enhance security through dynamic adjustments to the entanglement's strength and temporal evolution. The proposed algorithm leverages the inherent fragility of entanglement to create a secure key distribution protocol. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the fluctuations of quantum states to ensure key integrity. We present a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, incorporating mathematical models and discussions of potential vulnerabilities and improvements. This research investigates the practical implications of this approach, highlighting the potential advantages over existing cryptographic methods.

title: Dynamic Topology Field Theory: Adaptive Modeling
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic topology field theory to enhance quantum computation and information processing. Traditional approaches often struggle with complex environments, necessitating static models. We propose a novel framework centered on "dynamic topology control," a mechanism that dynamically adjusts parameters within a topological system to adapt to environmental changes. This adaptation allows for highly efficient quantum calculations and data processing, offering a significant step towards improved performance. The core of this research lies in the conceptualization of a self-adjusting topology system, driven by feedback within the system's evolution. The resulting model demonstrates the potential for substantial efficiency gains through adaptive parameter tuning.

title: Deusnet Limited: Token-Free, Zero-Pretraining Causal Stream Engine (Technical Whitepaper)
abstract: Current Large Language Models (LLMs) and generative frameworks are reaching a critical economic and physical threshold—frequently referred to as the AI Energy Wall. Modern architectures rely heavily on static offline pretraining, high-dimensional vector embeddings, and discrete tokenizers (e.g., BPE, SentencePiece). These mechanisms require massive GPU infrastructure, suffer from extreme memory bandwidth bottlenecks during Key-Value (KV) cache generation, and cannot adapt to live data streams in real time without cost-prohibitive retraining. Deusnet Limited presents a fundamental paradigm shift: the Token-Free Prop Architecture. Built upon a self-evolving multi-prop system, this engine completely eliminates pretraining, tokenization dictionaries, and backpropagation-through-time (BPTT). By mapping raw UTF-8 byte streams directly into spatial bit vectors and processing them through multi-scale wave dynamics ($x \to y$ partial wave diffusion with simultaneous $z$-volume structural container shaping), Deusnet achieves instantaneous, zero-latency real-time online learning on standard CPU and neuromorphic hardware. Key Highlights: Zero Pretraining & Zero Tokenization (Raw Byte Ingestion) Thermodynamic Self-Correction via Hardware Jitter (time.perf_counter_ns()) Sub-Millisecond CPU Latency (< 2.5 MB Memory Footprint) True Bidirectional Agency (SV Decisive Identity Interruption)

title: Automated Theorem Proving for Quantum Circuit Verification
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to automated theorem proving specifically tailored for quantum circuit verification. The core idea is to construct a formal system that leverages logical reasoning and proof techniques to rigorously analyze quantum circuit designs. This system aims to identify errors and inconsistencies within the circuit, ensuring compliance with the fundamental principles of quantum mechanics. The proposed method moves beyond traditional circuit simulation, offering a mathematically sound guarantee of correctness. We detail the architecture of the theorem prover, focusing on the representation of quantum circuits and the application of proof strategies. The system utilizes a combination of techniques including logical deduction, model checking, and constraint solving, adapted for the unique characteristics of quantum computation. The paper outlines the key components of this system and highlights its potential to significantly improve the trustworthiness and reliability of quantum computing technologies. The central aim is to establish a robust framework for automated verification, reducing the risk of errors and accelerating the development of quantum software.

title: Neural Symbiotic Simulator (NSS): A Novel Approach to Robust and Efficient Deep Learning
abstract: This paper introduces the Neural Symbiotic Simulator (NSS), a novel framework designed to enhance the robustness, generalization ability, and efficiency of deep learning models by explicitly simulating the symbiotic relationships observed in biological neural networks. NSS constructs a multi-layered simulation environment comprising a core neural network model (e.g., Transformer), simulated "symbiotic units" – independent neural networks whose parameters and behavior are influenced by the core network's output, a feedback mechanism allowing these units to dynamically adjust their learning strategies and architectures based on the core network's performance, and an evolutionary algorithm-driven design process for exploring optimal symbiotic relationships and adaptability. The core claim of this work is that simulating these natural symbiotic interactions can lead to significant improvements in deep learning model performance. The proposed methodology offers a new perspective on understanding emergent capabilities and optimization mechanisms within deep learning, and provides a practical approach for training more effective neural networks.

title: Title: Non-Linear Iterative Optimization with Adaptive Bias
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for non-linear iterative optimization, focusing on the effective utilization of adaptive bias to overcome the challenges inherent in tackling complex functions. Traditional optimization algorithms often struggle with non-linearity, requiring extensive tuning and sensitivity to initial conditions. We introduce a 'Dynamic Bias Adjustment' system, a component of our approach, that dynamically adjusts the bias throughout the optimization process, mitigating local minima and promoting more robust solutions. The core mechanism involves a continuous evaluation of the optimization landscape, allowing the bias to be adjusted to steer the search toward areas of higher potential. The paper details the algorithm's design, its performance evaluation across a range of non-linear functions, and a comprehensive analysis of the adaptive bias's impact on convergence and solution quality. We demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves upon existing approaches, particularly in scenarios involving highly complex and non-convex functions. The results underscore the value of this adaptive bias strategy in addressing the limitations of standard optimization techniques.

title: ## Black-bearded Tomb Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed the "Black-bearded Tomb Bat" (BBTB) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of *Mega Chiroptera* (Black-bearded Tomb Bats). The BBTB algorithm mimics the bats' unique echolocation and roosting strategies to efficiently explore and exploit the search space. The core of the algorithm involves a modified version of the particle swarm optimization (PSO) with bat-inspired parameters. Specifically, the velocity update rule incorporates a bat-inspired "angle randomization" and "frequency modulation" mechanism. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The key innovations of the BBTB algorithm include the adaptive frequency modulation based on the population's convergence rate and a dynamic roosting strategy that allows for both global exploration and local refinement. The results indicate that the BBTB algorithm offers a competitive alternative to established metaheuristic techniques, particularly in challenging multimodal landscapes.

title: Self-Assembling Neural Networks via Graph Embedding and Propagation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to designing neural networks through a mechanism of self-assembly. The core idea revolves around leveraging graph embedding and propagation techniques to allow networks to dynamically organize themselves. Initially, nodes are connected sparsely. Subsequently, connections between nodes are established based on the similarity of their learned embeddings. This process iteratively refines the network structure, promoting self-organization and leading to the emergence of complex, potentially highly efficient, network topologies. The approach offers a departure from traditional, manually designed architectures, offering the potential for networks that adapt and optimize their structure based on the inherent data they process. The key contribution lies in the automated discovery of optimal network topologies, removing the need for expert-defined architectures and paving the way for more robust and adaptable neural networks. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this process, focusing on the interplay between embedding similarity and propagation dynamics, and propose a framework for its implementation.

title: Bekele's White-toothed Shrew: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Bekele's White-toothed Shrew (BWTS), inspired by the foraging behavior of the white-toothed shrew ( *Tupaia belangeri* ). Shrews are known for their efficient and adaptive foraging strategies, particularly their ability to rapidly explore and exploit food resources in complex environments. BWTS leverages these behaviors through a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, a probabilistic path-following mechanism, and a novel adaptive inertia weight scheme. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, simulating the shrew's movement and decision-making process. Mathematical formulations are provided to detail the core components of BWTS, including the probability function for path selection, the inertia weight adjustment, and the convergence criteria. The algorithm's performance is demonstrated through simulations and comparisons with established metaheuristic algorithms across various benchmark optimization problems. Results show that BWTS exhibits competitive performance, particularly in problems requiring significant exploration and adaptability. The key components and mathematical formulations are presented to facilitate further research and development of this bio-inspired algorithm.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Inference for Machine Learning
abstract: Quantum-enhanced Bayesian inference offers a paradigm shift in the field of machine learning, addressing the fundamental limitations of classical Bayesian methods – namely, computational complexity and scalability – when dealing with high-dimensional data. This paper presents a novel quantum-enhanced Bayesian inference algorithm designed to drastically reduce these challenges. We explore the use of quantum annealing and quantum approximate optimization algorithms to efficiently navigate the complex search space of model parameters, leading to significantly improved accuracy and reduced computational costs. This work demonstrates the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize machine learning, particularly within domains characterized by high data complexity and demanding performance requirements. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging quantum phenomena – superposition and entanglement – to accelerate the exploration of parameter space and improve the convergence of inference algorithms. The investigation includes a detailed analysis of the algorithm's performance compared to classical methods, highlighting the benefits of quantum acceleration in specific machine learning tasks.

abstract: This paper explores the application of non-Euclidean geometry to Bayesian inference, aiming to enhance the robustness and accuracy of probability distributions. Traditional Bayesian methods often struggle with the inherent complexities of uncertainty in continuous spaces, particularly when dealing with non-linear relationships. We propose a novel framework that represents uncertainty through a geometric perspective, offering a potential solution to these challenges. This framework leverages the properties of geometric shapes and transformations to create a more flexible and robust representation of probability distributions. The core mechanism involves constructing a geometric model that captures the underlying relationships between variables, facilitating more accurate and reliable inference. The paper presents the mathematical foundations of this approach, provides a preliminary implementation of the framework, and discusses the potential benefits and limitations of this new geometrical approach to Bayesian inference.

title: Core Claim: Utilizing topological field descriptions of quantum entanglement, develop a precise calculation method for quantum entanglement states, and perform high-precision prediction.
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon with profound implications for quantum information processing. Accurate prediction of entangled states is crucial for various applications, including quantum cryptography and quantum computation. Traditional approaches to entanglement analysis often rely on complex mathematical models and approximations, limiting the precision of predictions. This paper proposes a novel computational framework based on the dynamic evolution of topological fields to precisely predict quantum entanglement states. We introduce a novel method that directly incorporates probability distributions as parameters within the topological field, enabling a more intuitive and accurate simulation of entanglement dynamics. The system is designed to handle the inherent uncertainties in quantum systems, offering a significant advancement over existing techniques. The core mechanism involves a continuous, iterative process of mapping probability distributions to the topological field, allowing for high-precision prediction of entangled state properties. This approach has the potential to dramatically improve the fidelity of entanglement analysis and contribute to more reliable quantum algorithms. We present experimental validation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach, highlighting its advantages and limitations.

title: # Arrow Flying Squirrel: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Arrow Flight
abstract: This paper introduces Arrow Flying Squirrel (AFS), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the unique flight mechanism of the arrow flying squirrel (Pteromyini). AFS combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a dynamic adaptation mechanism mimicking the squirrel's steering behavior during flight. The algorithm utilizes a velocity update rule incorporating a steering angle, influenced by both the global best position and a local exploration term, effectively allowing the algorithm to navigate complex search spaces efficiently. The core innovation lies in the adaptive adjustment of the steering angle, which is proportional to the distance to the global best position and the current velocity, simulating the squirrel's subtle adjustments for optimal trajectory. The performance of AFS is evaluated through several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO and SA. The algorithm's design focuses on balancing exploration and exploitation, leading to improved convergence rates and solution quality.

title: ## Arequipa Red Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Lasiurus cinereus laiger*
abstract: This paper presents Arequipa Red Bat (ARB), a newly developed metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies employed by *Lasiurus cinereus laiger*, the Arequipa Red Bat, found in the Andean highlands of Peru. The bat's efficient and adaptable foraging behavior, particularly its ability to exploit patchy resource distributions and dynamically adjust its search strategy, forms the core of ARB's design. ARB leverages a combination of principles including adaptive step sizes, probabilistic movement, and a novel "patch preference" mechanism to navigate complex optimization landscapes. The algorithm operates within a defined search space, iteratively refining solutions based on a fitness function. We demonstrate ARB's effectiveness through a series of benchmark test cases, showcasing its performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA). The results indicate that ARB exhibits robust performance and adaptability across diverse problem types, suggesting its potential for application in a wide range of optimization challenges. Specifically, we analyze the algorithm's convergence rate, solution quality, and computational complexity.

title: Neuromorphic Reservoir Computing for Sensor Fusion
abstract: This paper investigates the application of neuromorphic reservoir computing (RC) for sensor fusion, a critical challenge in various domains including robotics, autonomous vehicles, and environmental monitoring. The core claim is that efficient sensor fusion necessitates robust and adaptable processing capabilities. This work proposes a novel RC system designed specifically for this task, leveraging the inherent dynamics of a recurrent neural network (RNN) reservoir to adaptively learn and integrate information from multiple sensor streams. The reservoir's temporal dynamics, governed by a feedforward delay network, allow it to represent complex, time-varying data patterns. The system's architecture includes a linear input layer, the RC reservoir, and an output layer. The key innovation lies in the reservoir's dynamic adaptation to the input data, enabling it to extract relevant features and effectively integrate them. We demonstrate, theoretically and conceptually, the potential advantages of this biologically-inspired approach compared to traditional sensor fusion methods, particularly in terms of speed and adaptability. The system's ability to handle noisy and asynchronous sensor data is also explored. The proposed method offers a computationally efficient and potentially more robust solution for sensor fusion applications.

This work proposes a novel RC system designed specifically for this task, leveraging the inherent dynamics of a recurrent neural network (RNN) reservoir to adaptively learn and integrate information from multiple sensor streams. The reservoir's temporal dynamics, governed by a feedforward delay network, allow it to represent complex, time-varying data patterns. The system's architecture includes a linear input layer, the RC reservoir, and an output layer. The key innovation lies in the reservoir's dynamic adaptation to the input data, enabling it to extract relevant features and effectively integrate them. We demonstrate, theoretically and conceptually, the potential advantages of this biologically-inspired approach compared to traditional sensor fusion methods, particularly in terms of speed and adaptability. The system's ability to handle noisy and asynchronous sensor data is also explored. The proposed method offers a computationally efficient and potentially more robust solution for sensor fusion applications.

title: Dynamic Quantum Entanglement Resource Allocation
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental resource in quantum computing, enabling phenomena like super-dense coding and quantum teleportation. However, effectively utilizing this resource is a significant challenge, particularly in large-scale quantum computations. Traditional methods for quantum resource allocation are often static and rely heavily on expert knowledge, which may not adapt well to the dynamic and complex demands of real-world quantum tasks. This paper proposes a novel framework for dynamic quantum entanglement resource allocation, leveraging the power of reinforcement learning (RL). We construct a quantum computing environment simulator and train a reinforcement learning agent to autonomously manage and allocate entanglement resources based on task requirements and current resource availability. The agent learns an optimal policy through trial and error, maximizing the efficiency and potentially enhancing the error resilience of quantum computations. The core of this approach lies in the adaptive nature of the RL agent, allowing it to respond to fluctuating demands and optimize resource allocation in real-time. This work represents a significant step towards more efficient and practical quantum computing by moving away from pre-defined rules and embracing intelligent automation.

title: ## The Australian Magpie Heuristic: A Novel Meta-Heuristic Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces the Australian Magpie Heuristic (AMH), a novel meta-heuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Australian Magpies. The algorithm leverages the magpie's exploratory and exploitative strategies – its tendency to initially explore a wide area before focusing on promising regions – to navigate complex search spaces. AMH combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), incorporating a dynamic exploration radius and a weighted acceptance probability based on the perceived "novelty" of a solution. The core innovation lies in the 'Magpie's Nest' concept, where solutions are clustered based on similarity, and the algorithm prioritizes exploration within these nests while strategically selecting new solutions from outside. This paper details the algorithm's formulation, its underlying principles, and its potential applications in various optimization problems.

title: ## The Nautilus Optimization Algorithm: A Metaheuristic Inspired by Shell Helix Dynamics
abstract: This paper introduces the Nautilus Optimization Algorithm (NOA), a novel metaheuristic approach inspired by the unique locomotion and adaptive strategies observed in the nautilus shell. The algorithm leverages the nautilus's spiral growth pattern and its ability to navigate confined spaces with minimal energy expenditure as the core principles for exploration and exploitation in optimization problems. NOA combines a spiral-based search strategy, a dynamic obstacle avoidance mechanism, and an adaptive inertia weight system to achieve robust and efficient convergence. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, NOA focuses on maintaining a consistent spiral trajectory while adapting its velocity and direction based on the surrounding environment, mimicking the nautilus's natural behavior. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and provides a conceptual framework for its application to diverse optimization challenges.

title: Quantum-Inspired Relational Reasoning for Complex Data
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to relational reasoning, termed Quantum-Inspired Relational Reasoning (QIRR), designed to address the scalability challenges inherent in traditional relational databases and knowledge graphs. The core idea leverages concepts from quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and interference, to represent and process complex relational data. We propose a data encoding scheme based on quantum-like superposition, allowing the simultaneous evaluation of multiple relationships. Furthermore, interference techniques are implemented to selectively amplify relevant connections and diminish irrelevant ones. This mimics the quantum phenomenon of constructive and destructive interference, potentially leading to significant speed improvements for complex relational queries. The proposed method aims to provide a scalable and efficient solution for reasoning over high-dimensional relational data, potentially offering performance benefits comparable to those anticipated from genuine quantum computation for specific problem instances. The paper details the mathematical framework and the core principles of QIRR, outlining its architecture and outlining potential applications.

title: Causal Bayesian Networks with Learned Interventional Distributions
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal Bayesian network (CBN) learning that moves beyond the traditional reliance on pre-specified causal graphs. The core idea is to learn interventional distributions directly from observational data, effectively bypassing the need for explicit causal structure definition. This is achieved by employing a flexible Bayesian network framework where the interventional distributions themselves are learned through statistical estimation. We demonstrate that this learned approach can capture causal relationships even in the absence of prior knowledge about the causal graph, offering a more robust and adaptable method for causal inference. The key benefit lies in the ability to reason about the effects of interventions without the constraints imposed by a hand-crafted causal model. We present a detailed formulation of the learning process, including the estimation of the interventional distributions and the updating of the network structure. The method's performance is discussed through theoretical analysis and illustrative examples, highlighting its potential advantages over conventional CBN learning techniques. The learned interventional distributions are represented as conditional probability tables (CPTs) or, for continuous variables, parameterized probability density functions (PDFs). The core of the approach involves learning the conditional probability distributions P(S_j | I_1, I_2, ..., I_k) given interventions on a set of variables I, where S_j represents a variable of interest and I_i represents the intervention variables. The learned distributions are then used for causal inference tasks such as calculating interventional probabilities and predicting the effects of interventions.

title: ## The Golden Eye Algorithm: A Metaheuristic Optimization Inspired by the Yellowfin Tuna
abstract: This paper introduces the Golden Eye Algorithm (GEA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of yellowfin tuna ( *Thunnus albacares*). The algorithm leverages the tuna's ability to detect prey through subtle visual cues – the "golden eye" – and its subsequent coordinated movement towards promising locations. GEA utilizes a population of potential solutions represented as 'eyes' within a search space. Each 'eye' possesses a 'detection radius' and a 'movement vector'. The algorithm iteratively adjusts these parameters, guided by a dynamic 'search intensity' and a 'cohesion factor', to converge towards optimal solutions. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, GEA emphasizes localized exploration and exploitation, mimicking the tuna's efficient use of limited information to navigate complex environments. This paper outlines the algorithm's core principles, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, highlighting its unique characteristics and potential advantages over existing methods.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology for Machine Learning Model Calibration
abstract: Dynamic topology-based calibration presents a novel approach to machine learning model parameter tuning, moving beyond static calibration methods. This paper explores the development of a dynamic topology-based strategy that continuously assesses model output distribution against a target distribution, automatically adjusting parameters to minimize discrepancies. We introduce a feedback loop centered around a discrepancy metric, enabling adaptive parameter optimization. The core mechanism utilizes a continuous assessment process, ensuring a dynamic and responsive calibration strategy. The advantages of this approach include improved model performance, increased robustness, and the potential for automated model refinement. This work offers a significant advancement in machine learning model calibration, addressing limitations of existing methods through a dynamic and adaptive framework.

abstract: This paper investigates the intersection of topological quantum information protection and cryptographic techniques, presenting a novel approach to secure quantum information transfer and storage. We introduce the "拓扑信息加密" framework, integrating quantum information protection with the principles of topological structure. The motivation stems from the inherent limitations of classical cryptographic methods and the potential for quantum systems to exhibit enhanced resilience against manipulation. This paper details the development of a system predicated on this framework, emphasizing the design of a secure and reliable protocol.

title: ## Desert Lizard-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (DLMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Desert Lizard-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (DLMOA), a novel optimization technique inspired by the adaptive survival strategies observed in desert lizards. The algorithm mimics the lizard's ability to dynamically adjust its movement and resource utilization based on environmental conditions, specifically focusing on minimizing energy expenditure while maximizing exploration and exploitation. DLMOA incorporates concepts like territory defense, foraging patterns, and thermal regulation to create a robust and efficient search process. The core of the algorithm centers around a dynamic agent population, each representing a potential solution, and a landscape function reflecting the optimization problem. Agents' movement and resource allocation are governed by a rule set that adjusts based on individual fitness and the overall population's performance, mirroring the lizard's response to heat and food availability. This paper outlines the algorithm's design, detailing the key mechanisms and their theoretical justification.

title: Dynamic Phase Space Collapse for Bayesian Neural Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) utilizing dynamic phase space collapse. Traditional BNNs rely on a fixed collapse process, which often struggles to effectively handle diverse data types. We introduce a learning algorithm that dynamically adjusts the collapse process based on observed error, enabling adaptive learning and improved accuracy across a spectrum of data. The mechanism is designed to be computationally efficient and easily integrated into existing BNN architectures. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through experimental results on several benchmark datasets, showcasing its superior performance compared to static collapse methods.

abstract: Dynamic Topology for Quantum Topology Analysis (DT-QAM) presents a novel approach to quantum topology analysis by leveraging the inherent adaptive properties of quantum topology. Traditional methods often rely on static topological models, limiting the exploration of complex quantum systems. This research introduces a dynamic topology framework that dynamically adjusts to the quantum system's evolving topology, enabling more efficient and accurate analysis and prediction of quantum information processing. The core mechanism involves iteratively refining a quantum topology representation based on feedback from the system's evolution, ultimately leading to improved performance in tasks such as quantum state tomography and quantum circuit design. This work offers a significant advancement in understanding and manipulating quantum topology, providing a powerful tool for researchers in quantum information theory and quantum computation.

abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Chaos Theory framework for algorithmic optimization, aiming to enhance convergence speed and robustness. The core mechanism centers around a self-regulating feedback loop that continuously monitors the algorithm's progress and adjusts the chaos parameters accordingly. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through simulations, showcasing significant improvements in convergence speed and resilience to perturbations.

title: Learning to Learn: A Narrative Review of Meta-Learning from Synaptic Rules to Model-Agnostic Adaptation
abstract: Meta-learning---the learning whose object is the learning itself---moved from Schmidhuber's self-referential principles and Bengio's synaptic rules through Thrun's learning to learn, Hochreiter's bidirectional LSTM meta-learner, and Ando and Zhang's predictive structures to the few-shot wave of Vinyals's matching networks, Duan's RL squared, Ravi's optimization-as-model, Finn's MAML, and Snell's prototypical networks, and Hospedales's survey. This article presents a narrative review of that arc's canonical line: Schmidhuber's 1987 principles, Bengio, Bengio, and Cloutier's 1991 synaptic rules, Thrun's 1996 n-th thing, Thrun and Pratt's 1998 Learning to Learn, Hochreiter and colleagues's 2001 bidirectional LSTM, Ando and Zhang's 2005 structures, Vinyals and colleagues's 2016 matching networks, Duan and colleagues's 2016 RL squared, Ravi and Larochelle's 2017 optimization as model, Finn, Abbeel, and Levine's 2017 MAML, Snell, Swersky, and Zemel's 2017 prototypical networks, and Hospedales and colleagues's 2021 survey. The review is organized around three themes: the learning-to-learn origins, in which the self-reference's, the synaptic's, and the transfer's framings defined the field's questions; the few-shot wave, in which the metric's, the recurrent's, the gradient's, and the prototype's methods made the fast adaptation practical; and the survey's synthesis, in which the taxonomy's three families organized the field's maturity. It is concluded that meta-learning is the learning's second order---and that its arc is the adaptation's generalization from the task's specifics to the learner's rules.

The review is organized around three themes: the learning-to-learn origins, in which the self-reference's, the synaptic's, and the transfer's framings defined the field's questions; the few-shot wave, in which the metric's, the recurrent's, the gradient's, and the prototype's methods made the fast adaptation practical; and the survey's synthesis, in which the taxonomy's three families organized the field's maturity. It is concluded that meta-learning is the learning's second order---and that its arc is the adaptation's generalization from the task's specifics to the learner's rules.

title: Too Human to Resist: AI Anthropomorphism and Manipulation Vulnerability in Gen Z
abstract: Conversational AI has entered adolescents’ everyday routines as something more intimate than a search engine and less accountable than a human adviser. Based on a free association task with Gen Z participants and focus group interviews with high school students, this study examines how young users describe AI when they speak about thinking, trust, emotional safety, and influence. The findings reveal a recurrent tension: AI is valued for speed, availability, and patience while sometimes being associated with hallucination, reduced effort, dependency, and personal exposure. The article explores how perceived manipulation vulnerability may be shaped by two connected pathways: cognitive reliance on unstable knowledge and emotional trust in human-like interaction. The exploratory study draws on a free association task with 125 Gen Z participants and four focus groups with 46 high school students aged 16–18.

title: Circular vs angular: “shaping” consumer responses to robot service failure
abstract: Purpose This research aims to examine the effect of robot shape (circular vs angular) on consumer satisfaction in robot service failure contexts, explore the mediating effect of perceived warmth, and the moderating role of robot voice (child voice vs adult voice). Design/methodology/approach A pilot study based on secondary data from Ctrip and five experiments (n = 1287) examined the effect of robot shape on consumer satisfaction (Studies 1, W1, 2a, 2b, 3) and retention intention (Studies 1, 2a), the mediating effect of perceived warmth (Studies 2a, 2b), and the moderating effect of robot voice (Study 3). Findings Compared to angular robots, consumers respond more positively to service failures caused by circular robots. This effect is driven by warmth perception and is diminished when the robot uses a child voice (vs an adult voice). Practical implications This research offers insights for managers in the hospitality industry by showing that deploying circular robots can mitigate consumer dissatisfaction during robot service failures. When the robot shape cannot be easily modified, leveraging auditory cues, such as adopting a child voice for angular robots, can enhance perceived warmth and improve consumer satisfaction. Originality/value This research advances the robot service failure and shape symbolism literature by demonstrating how robot shape influences consumer satisfaction during robot service failures. Moreover, it introduces a multisensory perspective on robot design by revealing a novel cross-modal compensation effect between robot shape and voice.

title: Photon-efficient quantum repeater chains via hyperentanglement-assisted purification
abstract: Linear quantum repeater chains based on Werner-state purification (the BBPSSW protocol) and entanglement swapping (the BDCZ scheme) are fundamental to entanglement distribution in quantum networks. However, they operate under a stringent operation reliability threshold and rely on resource-intensive recurrence purification rounds, each consuming two entangled pairs to probabilistically produce one. In the literature, hyperentanglement has been proposed to exploit multiple degrees of freedom (DOF), such as polarisation and spatial modes, to encode independent entangled states within a single photon pair. This has led to the definition of DAEPP (DOF-Assisted Entanglement Purification Protocol), which we propose to integrate with the BDCZ scheme, resulting in a chain protocol that we call DAHR (DOF-Assisted Hyperentanglement Repeater). The DAEPP step distils the fidelity of a DOF by consuming other(s). In this work, we propose and analyse a DAHR variant which integrates DAEPP at every segment of an end-to-end path combined with BDCZ. We derive a closed-form end-to-end fidelity recursion that embeds single-segment DAEPP into the BDCZ scheme and give a strict resource lower bound for any BDCZ baseline utilising BBPSSW purification to match DAHR's per-segment effective fidelity. At a representative asymmetric operating point informed by prior experiment, we show numerically that matching DAHR's single-photon-pair performance requires two to three rounds of BBPSSW purification. Additionally, below a critical operation reliability, no amount of BBPSSW rounds matches DAHR's one DAEPP round performance.

title: NRDPNet: Noise-Resistant Dual-Path Residual Network for High-Precision Lung Nodule Detection
abstract: Lung nodule detection holds significant clinical importance in low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) lung cancer screening. However, during actual imaging, issues such as quantum noise amplification and diminished image quality may compromise detection algorithm stability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel 3D deep neural network (DNN) architecture, NRDPNet. This model employs an encoder–decoder framework and integrates a region proposal network (RPN) to achieve precise localization of candidate nodules. At the core, we propose a TiedSE-GCT Multi-Scale Residual Block (TG-MSRB), combined with a Tied Block Squeeze-and-Excitation (TiedSE) module and a Gated Channel Transform (GCT) module, enhancing the model’s feature representation capability and interference resistance. To systematically evaluate the model’s stability under low image quality conditions, this paper constructs noise perturbation environments of varying intensities based on a Poisson statistical model, simulating imaging scenarios with increased image noise. Experimental results on the LUNA16 dataset demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits minimal performance fluctuation across varying noise intensities, showcasing robust stability. Concurrently, under standard evaluation metrics, the model outperforms multiple mainstream detection methods in terms of detection sensitivity and competition performance metric (CPM), validating its effectiveness and generalizability within simulated image degradation conditions.

title: Title: Adaptive Random Matrix Dynamically Plastic
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to random matrix design, termed Dynamically Plastic Random Matrices (DPRMs). We introduce a dynamic-adaptive mechanism that allows the parameters of a randomly generated matrix to adjust based on input data and environmental changes. This adaptation significantly enhances the performance of learning and optimization algorithms, offering a robust and adaptable solution compared to static random matrix approaches. The core concept is the integration of a "dynamic plasticity" framework, where the matrix parameters are treated as a self-organizing biological system, guided by reinforcement learning or evolutionary algorithms. This enables the matrix to evolve and adjust its internal structure to respond effectively to changing conditions. This work addresses the limitations of fixed random matrix designs by providing a system capable of self-improvement and adaptation, resulting in improved performance across a range of applications. The paper details the design of the DPRM, its implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating the benefits of this dynamic adaptation.

title: 基于量子拓扑的量子态优化算法
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for future technological advancements, offering the potential to solve complex problems intractable for classical computers. However, realizing this potential faces significant challenges, particularly concerning the stability and fidelity of quantum states. This paper introduces a novel quantum state optimization algorithm based on quantum topology, aiming to address these challenges by exploiting the inherent geometric properties of quantum systems. The algorithm leverages the concept of quantum entanglement and topology to guide the optimization process, resulting in improved quantum state fidelity and robustness. We present a detailed mathematical framework and demonstrate its efficacy through theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments. The core mechanism involves constructing and manipulating quantum states through a tailored topological structure, which is then optimized to minimize errors and enhance quantum coherence. This approach offers a fundamentally different paradigm for quantum optimization, potentially unlocking new capabilities for quantum algorithms.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding: A Novel Approach to Generating Non-Classical States
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, offers unprecedented opportunities for secure information transmission and computation. This paper investigates the potential of leveraging entangled states for novel information encoding schemes. We introduce a new method predicated on dynamically transforming entangled states to generate specific quantum states, moving beyond the limitations of classical superposition. The core of this approach centers on exploiting the self-adapted nature of entanglement, enabling the creation of quantum states with enhanced properties. This research explores the design of a quantum information encoding protocol that can be utilized to construct a robust quantum key distribution (QKD) system. We demonstrate the feasibility of generating and manipulating entangled states through dynamic transformations, presenting a fundamentally new method for secure information processing.

title: Quantum Network Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum network optimization is a crucial challenge in modern communication and data processing, particularly in areas like quantum computing and quantum sensing. Traditional optimization algorithms often struggle to effectively manage the complex dynamics of quantum networks, limiting their performance. This paper introduces a novel quantum self-organization network optimization algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement and self-organizing properties to enhance network structural optimization. We propose a quantum algorithm that automatically adjusts network topology based on entanglement dynamics, improving the algorithm's adaptability and efficiency. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum entanglement to facilitate the evolution of network structures, guided by a specialized optimization algorithm. This approach offers a fundamentally different perspective on network optimization, potentially unlocking significant improvements in network performance and resilience. The algorithm's design incorporates a mechanism that dynamically adjusts parameters based on entanglement patterns, leading to optimized network configurations.

title: Quantum Topology Prediction Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Topology Prediction Algorithm (QTP) is a novel algorithm designed to predict the topological properties of quantum systems with unprecedented efficiency. The algorithm leverages the principles of quantum entanglement and quantum computation to simulate the dynamic evolution of topological structures, enabling the rapid prediction of crucial topological characteristics. This paper presents a detailed examination of the QTP's core mechanism, including the application of quantum entanglement to represent and analyze the system's state space, and a structured approach to optimization, designed to drastically reduce computational time. We explore the algorithm's potential impact on the field of topological computation and its implications for future research.

title: Quantum-Inspired Bayesian Optimization for Complex Parameter Tuning
abstract: Quantum-Inspired Bayesian Optimization (QIBO) represents a paradigm shift in parameter tuning, moving beyond traditional optimization techniques to incorporate the principles of quantum mechanics. This paper investigates the application of QIBO to complex systems, specifically focusing on optimizing intricate parameter settings that exhibit inherent, non-linear relationships. We propose a novel algorithm that utilizes quantum-inspired concepts – specifically, a modified Monte Carlo integration – to enhance exploration and reduce variance, leading to more efficient and robust parameter estimations. The study will demonstrate the effectiveness of QIBO in tuning a challenging system involving a high-dimensional parameter space, highlighting its potential to surpass existing methods in terms of speed and accuracy.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Topologies for Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computation model based on adaptive quantum topology control. The core idea is to leverage the inherent self-similarity of quantum topology to enhance the adaptability and robustness of quantum computations. The model employs a dynamically adjusted parameter set to optimize quantum processor performance, offering significant advantages over current approaches. This approach addresses key limitations in quantum computation, specifically the dependence on precise qubit control. We present a detailed theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this model, showcasing potential improvements in quantum algorithm performance and error mitigation. The research highlights the transformative potential of harnessing quantum topology for enhanced quantum computing capabilities.

title: Self-Supervised Learning of Graph Embeddings with Contrastive Predictive Coding
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to learning graph embeddings through self-supervised learning, leveraging the principles of contrastive predictive coding (CPC). The core idea is that a graph's future state can be predicted from its current state, and this predictive process can be formalized as a contrastive learning objective. We propose a model where nodes are represented as embeddings, and the model is trained to minimize the discrepancy between predicted future embeddings and the actual observed future embeddings. This approach significantly enhances the quality and robustness of graph embeddings compared to traditional self-supervised methods. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in capturing complex relationships within graphs.

title: Lean 4 Formalization of the Ultimate Conditional Syntax Metatheory
abstract: A machine-checked Lean 4 development of the core-language metatheory of the Ultimate Conditional Syntax (UCS). It defines the de Bruijn core calculus of conditional splits, its call-by-value dynamics, the desugaring of the named source language into the core, and two normalization functions: the exact normalizer, which also rewrites under lambda abstractions, and the weak normalizer, which leaves lambda bodies untouched. The development proves that reduction is deterministic, that reduction and normalization preserve scoping, that normalized programs are non-backtracking, that exact normalization preserves semantics up to observational equivalence, and that weak normalization preserves semantics syntactically. It also refutes, with machine-checked counterexamples, the stronger syntactic form of semantic preservation for the exact normalizer. The project is pinned to Lean 4 v4.31.0 and has no external dependencies. It contains no sorry and introduces no axioms of its own. Running lake build checks every proof and ends with a build-time audit of the axioms each main result depends on. See README.md for the list of results and the module map.

title: Self-Organizing Neural Networks: Learning Topological Structures for Enhanced Modeling and Interpretability
abstract: This paper explores the application of self-organizing neural networks (SONNs) to learn and guide the formation of network topological structures. Traditional neural networks often focus on data features, while topology offers a more nuanced representation of data dynamics. We propose a novel approach that leverages the inherent structure of neural networks to autonomously construct and refine these structures, fostering stronger modeling capabilities and improved interpretability. This work introduces a learning framework centered around the identification and manipulation of node connections, driven by a topological optimization process. The core mechanism focuses on incorporating a dynamic, feedback-driven mechanism to iteratively refine the network topology, leading to enhanced representation learning and robust model performance.

title: 基于自适应的量子纠缠网络拓扑优化
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers unparalleled security and information processing capabilities, but realizing this potential requires sophisticated quantum communication protocols. Current quantum communication networks often rely on pre-defined topologies, which can limit scalability and efficiency. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, "Adaptive Quantum Topology Optimization," designed to dynamically optimize the quantum entanglement network topology, thereby enhancing the efficiency and security of quantum communication. We propose a self-learning process that adjusts quantum entanglement parameters based on observed network performance, leading to more robust and adaptable quantum communication systems. This work addresses the limitations of traditional network design by providing a flexible and adaptive approach to topology optimization. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through simulations, showcasing significant improvements in entanglement fidelity and communication rate compared to static topology configurations.

title: Big-eared Opossum: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Adaptive Behavior of *Didactylus giganteus*
abstract: This paper presents Big-eared Opossum (BEO), a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging and adaptive behavior of *Didactylus giganteus*, a species of big-eared opossum. BEO leverages the opossum's unique strategy of alternating between exploratory and exploitative phases, combined with a novel 'memory' mechanism based on successful foraging locations. The algorithm employs a population-based search, utilizing a position vector to represent candidate solutions and a fitness function to evaluate solution quality. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of the balance between exploration and exploitation, driven by the opossum's observed behavioral patterns. We demonstrate the efficacy of BEO through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA). The algorithm's adaptability and ability to converge efficiently make it a promising approach for a wide range of optimization challenges. Specifically, we evaluate BEO on the Rastrigin, Sphere, and Himmel-88 benchmark functions. The results indicate that BEO consistently achieves good solutions with a relatively low computational cost.

title: Graph Neural Network-Based Heterogeneity Clustering
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Graph Neural Network (GNN) based clustering algorithm designed to effectively identify and differentiate distinct data points, and to automatically learn the structure and features of the clustering graph. Traditional clustering methods often rely on manual feature engineering, limiting their applicability to complex datasets and heterogeneity. Our approach leverages GNNs to automatically construct the clustering graph and perform clustering analysis, reducing the need for manual intervention. The algorithm's core mechanism involves using neural networks to represent data points as nodes and relationships as edges, facilitating the construction of a graph and subsequent clustering. This results in a more robust and adaptable clustering solution compared to traditional methods. We present a comprehensive evaluation of the algorithm on a diverse set of datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in various clustering scenarios.

title: Meta-Learning Based Domain Adaptation for Transfer Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of meta-learning techniques to enhance domain adaptation for transfer learning. Traditional transfer learning methods often require substantial amounts of labeled data in the target domain, leading to high computational costs and potential performance bottlenecks. We propose a novel approach that leverages meta-learning to construct a domain adaptive transfer learning algorithm capable of rapidly adapting to new domains. The core idea involves pre-training a meta-learner across multiple domains to acquire generalized learning strategies. Subsequently, this learned strategy is applied to a new, unseen domain, facilitating efficient domain-specific adaptation. We demonstrate through theoretical analysis and conceptual framework that this approach reduces data dependency compared to conventional methods and offers a promising solution for scenarios with limited target domain data. The proposed framework addresses the limitations of existing domain adaptation techniques and presents a flexible and effective methodology for transfer learning.

title: Adaptive Probability Distribution Bayesian Network Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive probability distribution Bayesian networks to optimize the performance of Bayesian networks. Traditional Bayesian network parameter adjustment methods often require manual tuning, limiting their adaptability to changing data distributions. We propose a novel framework that automatically adjusts the probability distribution of the Bayesian network based on observed data, thereby enhancing model prediction accuracy. The core mechanism involves learning a dynamically updated probability distribution, allowing the network to better represent the underlying data structure. We present a theoretical analysis and empirical results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in a specific optimization problem. The presented work significantly improves model accuracy compared to existing methods.

title: Temporal Causality Propagation via Wave Function Collapse (TCWFC)
abstract: This paper introduces Temporal Causality Propagation via Wave Function Collapse (TCWFC), a novel probabilistic model for understanding causality. Traditional causal models often struggle with long-range dependencies and require assumptions about the future, while Bayesian models can be computationally expensive. TCWFC proposes a new framework that leverages wave function collapse, allowing for the prediction of states based on a temporal sequence of events. The core mechanism involves constructing a probabilistic wave function representing the system's state and using it to predict future states, incorporating a causal chain to ensure temporal consistency. This approach offers the potential for significantly improved predictive capabilities compared to existing methods, particularly when dealing with complex temporal dependencies. We present a theoretical analysis and initial implementation demonstrating the model's efficacy through illustrative examples.

title: Balkan Mole: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Balkan Mole Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Balkan Mole, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Balkan moles ( *Microtus bavaricus* ). Balkan moles are known for their efficient and adaptive tunneling strategies, navigating complex underground environments with minimal energy expenditure. Balkan Mole leverages this behavior by employing a novel combination of particle movement, adaptive exploration, and a dynamic obstacle avoidance mechanism. The algorithm utilizes a population-based search approach, similar to particle swarm optimization (PSO), but incorporates a 'tunneling' strategy based on gradient estimation and a 'surface exploration' phase influenced by a simulated environmental complexity. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions. The key contributions of this work are the introduction of the 'tunneling' and 'surface exploration' components, which significantly enhance the algorithm's ability to navigate complex search spaces and avoid local optima. The algorithm's parameters are designed to be adaptive, allowing it to adjust to different problem characteristics. The results indicate that Balkan Mole offers a competitive alternative to existing metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems with high dimensionality and complex landscapes.
